description: THE ROLE We're a small team of 3 managing content production across a growing client portfolio - blog posts, landing pages, Google Business posts, press releases, and more. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Review AI-generated drafts for tone, clarity, structure, and readability — and make them sound like a real person wrote them - Strengthen blog post conclusions, add missing sections to landing pages, and sharpen calls-to-action that fall flat - Edit Google Business posts, press releases, service pages, and blog articles across multiple industries and brand voices - Catch templated, lifeless language that slips through automation and replace it with writing that actually lands - Ensure content meets basic on-page SEO standards: proper heading hierarchy, natural keyword integration, and internal linking opportunities - Flag structural issues in longer-form content (not just line edits) and propose improvements before anything ships - Sometimes, you have to write content from scratch. WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR Must Have - Strong copywriting and editorial instincts - this is the job - Proven experience writing and editing blog posts, landing pages, or web copy - Comfort editing AI-generated drafts without becoming dependent on them - Excellent command of English grammar and style - A genuine intolerance for weak, templated, or hollow writing - Working knowledge of on-page SEO basics (headings, keywords, interlinks) Nice to Have - Experience with Google Business Profile content - Multi-industry writing background - Familiarity with press release conventions - Previous work in an agency or content ops environment You'll Thrive Here If... - You can tell the difference between content that's technically correct and content that's actually good - You take ownership. If it ships under your review, it reflects your standard - You find templated AI output incomplete and frustrating, not convenient Work Setup Work is fully asynchronous, but the nature of the pipeline means most content will be ready for review in the evening. Expect your active window to fall around 5:00–9:00 PM on working days, since that's when the team wraps output. If you're a night owl or just prefer evening work, this fits naturally. CONTENT TYPES YOU WILL HANDLE Blog posts, Service & location landing pages, Google Business posts, Press releases, Supporting web copy TO APPLY: - Send a short note about your editorial background along with writing samples. - Write an interesting, eye-catching subject line - I'll ignore you if you write something generic.

description: About Us We're a multi-brand DTC e-commerce company doing ~$300K/month. We run paid ads on Meta at scale and we're growing fast. We're not an agency. We own our brands. That means when you write a winning ad, you see the spend scale, the ROAS climb, and the brand grow. Your work has real impact and you stay with us long-term. We're hiring ONE Creative Strategist to work directly with the founder. This is a long-term role, not a project. If you want stability, growth, and to actually OWN the creative output of a real brand, keep reading. What You'll Actually Do You are the engine behind every ad we run. You research, you think, you write, and you brief our editors. The editors execute YOUR ideas. You will: Write hooks, ad concepts, and short-form scripts (15s, 30s, 60s, and longer VSL formats) Develop angles — new mechanisms, new avatars, new pain points, new positioning we haven't tested yet Mine customer reviews, comments, and competitor ads to find winning insights and translate them into ads Brief our video editors with clear, executable creative briefs (we'll teach you our brief format) Analyze ad performance and tell us what to double down on, what to iterate, what to kill Build creative variations from winners — take one winning ad and turn it into 10–20 meaningful variations Research customer psychology using reviews from Amazon, Trustpilot, Reddit, and our own product pages Manage the creative pipeline in Google Sheets / Notion (briefs, deadlines, asset tracking, performance) Stay on top of competitor activity — what new ads are running, what offers are tested, what's scaling The founder will work alongside you on strategy. But you own the creative output. If our ads suck, that's on you. If they win, that's on you too — and we pay accordingly. Who This Is For You are right for this role if: You have at least 1 year of hands-on experience writing ads, hooks, and concepts for DTC or e-commerce brands. Not just "social media posts." Direct response paid ads. You can show us ads you wrote that ran on Meta or TikTok with real spend behind them You speak fluent written English and your writing has voice, rhythm, and persuasion — not robotic AI output You're obsessed with customer psychology. You actually enjoy reading 100 reviews to find the one phrase that becomes the hook. You're organized to a fault. Briefs go out on time, files named properly, sheets updated daily. You can write FAST. A new hook in 10 minutes, not 2 hours. A full 30s script in 30 minutes. You want to learn DTC marketing at a high level over 1–2 years and grow with one company. You can work 30–40 hours/week consistently. You are NOT right for this role if: You're a graphic designer, video editor, or general VA looking to pivot. This is a writer + strategist role. You write generic "benefit list" ads. We need angles, hooks, narratives — not bullet points. You can't show real ads you wrote. Portfolio is mandatory. You're using AI to write your application but couldn't defend your own answer live on a call. You want to run 5 client gigs on the side. We need focus. Compensation Hourly: $5–8/hour depending on experience and portfolio strength Hours: 30–40 hrs/week (full-time) Schedule: Flexible. Some overlap with European hours required (5 hours/day minimum overlap). Performance bonus: After 90 days, you earn a bonus every time one of your ads scales past a spend threshold at positive ROAS. Real money on top of base. We pay extra for winners. Growth path: Strong performers move to $7–10/hour within 6 months and own a full brand inside the company within 12 months. We pay on time. Every time. How to Apply (Read Carefully — Most Applicants Will Skip This) We get a lot of AI-generated applications. We can spot them in 10 seconds and we delete them. Here's what we actually want: 1. Put the word "octopus" as the first word of your application. This tells us you read the post. 2. Pick ONE ad fro ---------- ta Ad Library (www.> >facebook .com /ads/library) — any DTC brand, any niche. Then answer in your own words (NOT ChatGPT): a) What is the hook in the first 3 seconds and why does it work? b) Who is the target customer (avatar) and what is the main pain point or desire being triggered? c) Write 3 alternate hooks you would test against this ad. Real hooks, written out as you would write them for a script. d) What angle would you test next to improve performance (new avatar, new mechanism, new positioning)? Keep it tight. 200–300 words total. We care about your THINKING and your WRITING, not the length. 3. Share your portfolio. Send 2–3 examples of ads, hooks, scripts, or concepts YOU wrote that ran for real brands. Drive link, Notion page, or PDF — whatever works. No portfolio = no interview. 4. Tell us: Your hourly rate (within $5–8) Your weekly availability (hours/week) Your WhatsApp number How many years you've specifically written ads, hooks, or scripts for paid social Which brands or industries you've written for One sentence: why this role specifically, not just "any job" What Happens Next If your application is strong, we send you ONE paid test brief — You write hooks, a script, and a short concept rationale. If we like you, you can be working within 1 week. What We're NOT Not an agency. You work with the founder directly. Not a "job mill." We hire ONE person at a time and we keep them for years. title: Amazon/Walmart Product Researcher for Live Deal Website
job_title: Amazon/Walmart Product Researcher for Live Deal Website
description: I run an online deals website and deal-alert groups. I am looking for a fast, focused worker who can help find real Amazon/Walmart deals and prepare them for posting. This is not just a Shopify product listing job. The most important part of this job is finding good, post-worthy deals quickly. Main Responsibilities: Watch deal websites, Telegram channels, Amazon, Walmart, and other deal sources. Find strong Amazon/Walmart deals that are actually worth posting. Check if the price is truly good, not just “cheap.” Make sure deals are fresh/current, preferably price drops from today. Avoid old price drops, weak discounts, random junk products, and products with poor reviews. Prefer brand-name products when possible, but unknown brands can be considered if the deal is very strong, the reviews look good, and the product is useful. Avoid niche replacement parts or accessories that only work if someone already owns a specific product. Check if we posted the same or similar product recently. Prepare deals quickly with a clean title, sale price, regular price, coupon info, and clear instructions. Post deals to Shopify and share them to WhatsApp/social media. Work fast and stay focused during the full shift. What I Need: I need someone with strong deal judgment. You must understand the difference between a cheap product and a real deal. A good deal is usually a useful, complete product with a fresh price drop, strong discount, good reviews/brand, and real value for our audience. I do not want random junk, niche replacement parts, old price drops, weak discounts, or products that only a few people can use. Brand-name products are preferred, but unknown brands are okay when the discount is very strong, the reviews look good, and there are no better deals available. A strong deal can be: 50% off or more on a useful product 70% off or more on a very strong deal Sometimes 30% off if it is a popular brand, expensive item, household item, toy, clothing, baby item, electronics, or something people regularly buy But the discount must be real and the product must be worth posting. This job is not about sending many random links. Weak deals do not count. I need quality and speed together. Important Performance Expectations: When deal sources are active, I expect steady output. The target is around 10–16 quality deal submissions per hour, depending on how active the sources are. Sending only 4–5 deals per hour is usually not enough when other deal sites are actively posting. Sending many weak/junk deals just to show quantity is not acceptable. I would rather get 8 strong deals than 20 bad ones. Before sending/posting a deal, check that the price, coupon, promo code, and discount are still working now. Good Experience To Have: Please mention if you have experience with any of these: Amazon product research Walmart product research Keepa Online arbitrage Retail arbitrage Amazon FBA product sourcing Shopify product posting Affiliate/deal websites Telegram or ---------- deal posting Social media posting Direct deal-hunting experience is a big plus, but it is not required if you are smart, fast, focused, and willing to learn. Required Skills: Fast computer skills Good English reading and writing Strong attention to detail Ability to work without constant reminders Good product judgment Ability to follow instructions exactly Fast response time Reliable attendance Focused work during shift hours Work Hours: All hours are in U.S. New York Time Zone. These hours are non-negotiable. Sunday: 2:30 PM – 10:30 PM Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday: 4:30 PM – 10:30 PM, sometimes until 11:00 PM Saturday night in winter: around 6:30 PM – 11:30 PM Saturday night in summer: around 9:30 PM – 11:30 PM or 11:45 PM Internet, Power, and Backup Requirements: Because this is a live deal-alert job, reliable attendance and connection are very important. You must have: Stable home internet Backup internet, such as mobile hotspot or a second internet option Backup power, such as a generator, power station, or UPS A work location with limited power outages/blackouts Ability to stay online during the full shift without frequent disconnections Please do not apply if you regularly lose power or internet during work hours. Phone Requirement: You must have a good, up-to-date smartphone with fast mobile internet. Your phone must be able to: Run WhatsApp, Telegram , Shopify, browser, and social media apps smoothly Receive and send deal alerts quickly Be used as a mobile hotspot if home internet goes down Stay charged during the full shift Handle fast posting without freezing or lagging Trial Test: Before hiring, I will give a paid trial task. You may be asked to review deal links and choose which ones are worth posting, which ones should be skipped, and explain why. I am looking for someone who can think like this: “This is a good brand.” “This discount is strong.” “This product is useful for families.” “This looks cheap but it is junk.” “This is only a replacement part, so I would skip it.” “This was probably posted recently.” “This should be posted now before it sells out.” Starting pay: $3.25/hour during trial. Pay can increase to $3.50/hour after 12–14 weeks based on speed, deal quality, accuracy, focus, and attendance. Bonuses available for excellent performance. Bonuses may be available for excellent performance in busy seasons. We also provide one week of paid vacation twice per year. To Apply: Please answer these questions: 1) Have you done Amazon, Walmart, Keepa, online arbitrage, product research, or deal research before? 2) What tools have you used? 3) How fast can you work while staying accurate? 4) Are you comfortable being measured by both speed and quality? 5) Are you available to work the hours listed above in U.S. New York Time? 6) What phone model do you use? 7) Do you have fast mobile data? 8) Can your phone be used as a hotspot if your home internet goes down? 9) Please send a screenshot of your home internet speed test. 10) Please send a screenshot of your mobile internet speed test. 11) What is your backup internet option? 12) What is your backup power option? 13) How often do you usually have power outages or internet problems? 14)What city/province in the Philippines do you work from? Send one example of a product you think is a strong deal and explain why. Please do not apply if you only want a simple copy/paste job. I need someone who can find quality deals fast and stay focused.

description: I run an online deals website and deal-alert groups. I am looking for a fast, focused worker who can help find real Amazon/Walmart deals and prepare them for posting. title: Short-Term Rental Pricing Strategist & Operations Manager
job_title: Short-Term Rental Pricing Strategist & Operations Manager
description: We are a family-owned short-term rental business based in Northern Greece (Thessaloniki coast). We operate 2 beachfront apartments in the Thessaloniki area of Northern Greece, both connected on ---------- with 9.8+ guest review scores. We are launching on Airbnb soon. The business is run by a brother-and-sister team — we handle everything on the ground ourselves (guest experience, cleaning, check-ins, maintenance). What we are missing is someone with real strategic expertise who can build our pricing strategy AND make sure the day-to-day operations behind the scenes run smoothly. We are not a corporation. We are a family that takes pride in our properties and our guests. We are looking for someone who treats this like a partnership, not just a task list. If you are the kind of person who genuinely enjoys figuring out why one listing outperforms another and what to do about it — and who also gets satisfaction from knowing the numbers are accurate and the calendar is tight — you will enjoy working with us. ABOUT THE ENGAGEMENT This role has two phases: Phase 1 — Setup, Strategy Build & Systems Check (First 10–20 days) This phase will be heavier in hours (15–20 hours/week). During this time, you will audit our full ---------- setup, conduct deep competitor research, review our current pricing and rate structure, and deliver a complete pricing strategy and operational recommendations for both apartments. You will also check that our ---------- infrastructure is solid — extranet settings, rate plans, calendar configuration, payment setup, promotion structure, cancellation policies, and anything else that needs to be cleaned up or optimized. You will learn our P&L tracking system and begin logging reservation data accurately. Both apartments are connected on ---------- , so you need to understand how multi-property setups work. Phase 2 — Ongoing Summer Operations (4 months: June–September) If the strategy you deliver in Phase 1 is strong and we work well together, you stay on as our Apartment Pricing, Strategy & Operations Manager for the full summer season. During this phase, hours will be 10–15 per week depending on the needs. You will own weekly competitor monitoring, rate adjustments, performance reporting, calendar management, P&L tracking, and ongoing strategic recommendations. Peak summer in our area is intense — high demand, fast-moving competitor pricing, and every night counts. We need someone who stays sharp throughout and keeps the machine running behind the scenes. WHO THIS ROLE IS FOR This role is for someone who has spent at least 2 years inside the ---------- and/or Airbnb ecosystem from the host or property management side. Someone who already knows how discount stacking works, how Genius and mobile rates affect visibility, how to read the Booking extranet analytics, and how to build a pricing strategy that balances occupancy with profit. Someone who can look at 10 competitor listings and tell us exactly where we stand and what to do about it. And someone who understands that strategy means nothing if the calendar has errors, the P&L is wrong, or a reservation falls through the cracks. We do not need ideas on a whiteboard. We need someone who turns expertise into action — specific rate recommendations, specific changes to our extranet, specific moves based on what competitors are doing this week — while also making sure the operational foundation underneath is solid and accurate. WHO THIS ROLE IS NOT FOR This is NOT a general virtual assistant position. We are not looking for someone to only answer guest messages or do basic admin. This is NOT for someone who has only managed social media or written listing descriptions. We need analytical thinking and operational precision, not copywriting. This is NOT for someone who will wait for us to tell them what to do. We need someone who brings the plan to us and keeps the business running proactively. This is NOT for beginners who want to "learn about short-term rentals." We need proven hands-on experience. If you cannot explain the difference between effective discount percentage and nominal discount percentage, or you have never built a competitor pricing comparison, or you have never maintained a financial tracker for a rental property, this role is not the right fit. WHAT YOU WILL OWN ---------- Infrastructure Audit & Setup Review our full ---------- extranet setup for both connected apartments Check and optimize: rate plans, room configuration, cancellation policies, payment settings, promotion structure, Genius and mobile rate setup, calendar accuracy, content completeness Identify anything that is misconfigured, missing, or hurting our visibility and conversion Deliver a clear list of fixes with priority order and implement them (or guide us through implementation) Competitor Research & Market Intelligence Identify and track our top 10–12 competitors in the Perea / Neoi Epivates / Thessaloniki coast area Build and maintain a competitor tracking report: nightly rates (weekday/weekend/seasonal), discount strategies, review scores, listing quality, amenities, occupancy patterns Update this research weekly and deliver a brief written summary of what changed and what it means for us Monitor new listings entering our market and flag any threats Pricing Strategy & Rate Architecture Develop a full pricing plan for both apartments across the year: peak season, shoulder season, off-season, holidays, weekends Recommend our base nightly rates, discount structure (Genius, mobile, non-refundable, weekly, monthly), and minimum stay rules Advise on when to activate or pause specific promotions and rate plans Analyze how our current pricing is performing — are we leaving money on the table or pricing ourselves out? Deliver a monthly pricing review with clear, actionable recommendations P&L Tracking & Financial Operations Log every reservation into our P&L tracking spreadsheet accurately and completely (we have a detailed model already built with Greek tax logic — environmental fee, city tax, VAT, commission, bank charges, utilities, cleaning, maintenance reserve, and income tax) Ensure the numbers match what ---------- and Airbnb report — no discrepancies, no missing reservations Track net profit per reservation and per night for each apartment separately Maintain the monthly summary and year-to-date financial view Flag any reservation where the net profit falls below our minimum target so we can investigate and adjust Deliver a clean, accurate monthly P&L report for each apartment and combined Calendar & Booking Operations Keep the ---------- and Airbnb calendars accurate and synchronized at all times — zero double bookings Review upcoming reservations weekly: confirm dates are correct, rates match our strategy, no conflicts or errors Flag check-in/check-out overlaps that could create turnover problems (e.g., same-day checkout and check-in with no cleaning window) Monitor for cancellations and immediately flag freed-up dates so we can adjust pricing to resell them Ensure the overall apartment management flow runs smoothly from a systems perspective — if something is broken or inefficient in the booking pipeline, we expect you to catch it and raise it Revenue Reporting & Performance Tracking Track our key metrics: ADR, occupancy rate, net revenue per night, effective discount %, commission impact Flag occupancy gaps early and recommend tactical rate adjustments to fill them Provide a monthly performance report comparing our actual results to competitor benchmarks and to our own targets Strategic Advisory Deliver a 90-day pricing roadmap based on your initial competitor research and market analysis Recommend which ---------- programs and promotions are worth participating in and which are not Advise on our Airbnb launch pricing strategy Identify opportunities we are missing — country rates, early-bird discounts, last-minute deals, minimum stay optimization WHAT WE PROVIDE Full access to our ---------- extranet and Airbnb dashboard A detailed competitor research spreadsheet template (ready to use) A complete financial P&L model with Greek tax logic built in (you do not need to build it — you need to maintain it accurately) A revenue calculator that models discount stacking, commission, and net profit Owners who are engaged, responsive, and act fast on good recommendations A family business environment where your work has direct, visible impact GROWTH OPPORTUNITY We want to be transparent about what this could become. If this engagement goes well over the summer, there is a real opportunity to grow beyond our two apartments. We are connected with other property owners in the same area who are interested in professional pricing, strategy, and operations support for their own ---------- listings. We would be happy to introduce you and help you build a client base in our market. The right person could turn this into a steady, multi-property engagement across the Thessaloniki coast. But first, let us see what you can do with our two. REQUIREMENTS Minimum 2 years of hands-on experience with ---------- and/or Airbnb from the host, co-host, or property management side You have personally set up or managed rate plans, promotions, and pricing strategies (not just guest messaging) You have maintained financial records, P&L tracking, or revenue reporting for rental properties Strong analytical skills — you are comfortable with spreadsheets, data, and numbers Detail-oriented and accurate — our P&L model has precise tax calculations and we need the data entered correctly You can write a clear, concise report in English that a non-technical person can understand and act on Reliable internet and availability to overlap with European time zone (CET) for regular check-ins PREFERRED Experience with PriceLabs, Beyond Pricing, Wheelhouse, or AirDNA Experience with European or Mediterranean short-term rental markets Understanding of OTA commission structures and how they affect net revenue Experience managing pricing and operations across multiple connected properties on ---------- Experience with multi-platform calendar synchronization WHAT WE EXPECT Week 1–2: Complete ---------- infrastructure audit and competitor research delivered for both apartments. P&L tracker set up with all existing reservations logged. Week 3–4: Full pricing strategy and rate architecture recommended, with specific numbers and rate plans. Calendars verified and synced. Month 2: Weekly competitor updates and calendar checks running on schedule. P&L tracker accurate and up to date. First monthly performance and financial report delivered. Month 3: Measurable improvement in either ADR, occupancy, or net revenue per night compared to Month 1. Clean financial records with zero discrepancies. HOW TO APPLY Send us: Which ---------- or Airbnb properties you have managed — how many listings, and what was your specific role in pricing, strategy, and operations (not just guest communication or cleaning coordination) One example of a pricing decision you made that improved revenue or occupancy — what did you change, why, and what was the result Have you maintained P&L records or financial tracking for rental properties? If yes, briefly describe what you tracked and how Your availability and expected hourly rate Short, specific answers beat long generic ones. We read every application carefully.

title: Maintenance Coordinator - Property Management
description: Maintenance Coordinator (Virtual) US Residential Property Management | Remote (Philippines) | Full-Time Contractor QUICK FACTS Title: Maintenance Coordinator (Virtual) Reports To: Assistant Property Manager (escalation & approvals) Location: Remote (Philippines). US Central business-hours overlap required. Type: Full-time contractor (~40 hrs/week) Schedule: Monday–Friday, 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM Central (US business hours) Compensation: $1,800–2,100/mo USD (commensurate with experience) + 13th month pay (paid in December, prorated by tenure) Start Date: ASAP ABOUT US We are a growing Austin, Texas–based residential property management company managing 400+ doors — single-family homes and duplexes — across the greater Austin Metro area. We are committed to delivering an exceptional, hands-off ownership experience and great service to our residents. We run on AppFolio and are scaling deliberately, through systems, accountability, and talented people rather than constant management oversight. Every member of our team is expected to use AI daily to work faster, more accurately, and more independently. THE ROLE The Maintenance Coordinator owns the end-to-end resolution of maintenance across our portfolio — from intake to closeout — with minimal hand-holding. You are the single point of accountability for work orders: you triage them, coordinate vendors, communicate with residents and owners, and drive each one to completion within target timelines. You perform your own due diligence and bring decisions to your approver as a clean Yes/No or A/B/C question with full context attached — never an open-ended "what should I do?" This is not a passive ticket-routing role. We are not looking for a dispatcher; we are looking for someone who owns outcomes. This is an individual-contributor role — you personally own and execute the maintenance workflow end to end. You will make sound judgment calls within defined authority limits, anticipate problems before they become emergencies, keep meticulous records, and use AI tools to multiply your output. If you need to be told what to do every day, this is not the right fit. WHAT YOU WILL OWN Work Order Management -Triage and prioritize all incoming work orders in AppFolio: occupied properties first, then vacant, then annual inspections — adjusting for safety or legal urgency (a leak, no-AC in summer, or fire hazard always moves up). -Assign new work orders the same day they are received. -Maintain a continuously updated, color-coded, priority-tagged work-order tracker (with work-order age) so nothing slips and weekly reviews are never a last-minute scramble. -Drive every work order to closeout as quickly as possible — target under 7 days — and keep aged (7+ day) open orders to a minimum. Vendor & Repair Coordination -Source, schedule, and follow up with vendors (plumbers, HVAC, electricians, handymen, etc.); confirm scope, negotiate pricing, and verify quality on completion. -Gather and review estimates and photos before requesting any approval — always get the full picture first. -Maintain accurate, current vendor records, including W-9s, certificates of insurance (COIs), and pricing agreements. -Process and route vendor invoices within 2 business days of receipt. Resident & Owner Communication -Respond to resident and owner maintenance inquiries promptly and professionally across all channels. -For emergencies, call the resident within 30 minutes of receipt and notify them immediately once a vendor is scheduled. -Keep communication clear and professional (no slang, emojis, or "LOL"). Use AI to polish drafts before sending. -Read and correctly apply the lease on every relevant work order — the lease defines who is responsible for a repair, what the resident is owed, and the limits of your authority. You are expected to check the lease before making determinations, not after. Turnovers, Make-Readies & Inspections -Coordinate make-ready walks within 1 business day of move-out; drive make-readies to completion in a 7–10 business-day target window. -Collaborate with leasing and field teams on turnover work and move-in repairs. -Coordinate annual inspections and any follow-up work they surface. Preventive & Seasonal Readiness -Drive seasonal property readiness: freeze prep, HVAC inspections, pest control, and similar recurring work. -Anticipate weather-sensitive issues (a Texas freeze or heat wave) and get ahead of them. Utilities & Accounting Support -Assist with paying utility bills online and coordinating utilities during turnovers. -Support the Accounting team with collecting invoices and vendor invoice adjustments when needed. Documentation & SOPs -Save and correctly label all photos (work-order #, property) in JPEG format so anyone on the team can find them. -Keep your SOP wikis clear and current. The standard: could another tea ---------- mber run this process from your documentation with little to no further support? SUCCESS METRICS (KPIs) -New work orders assigned: Same day -Emergency work orders: Call resident within 30 minutes; notify when vendor scheduled -Follow-up on open WOs (vendor/resident): Every 1–2 business days until confirmed -Work order closeout: As soon as possible; within 7 days -Make-ready walk: Within 1 business day of move-out -Make-ready completion: 7–10 business days post move-out -Vendor invoices processed: Within 2 business days of receipt -Aged work orders (7+ days): Kept to a minimum AUTHORITY & DECISION RIGHTS -Repairs $1,000 or under: Full authority — use your best judgment, no approval required. -Repairs over $1,000: Escalate to your approver with full context (owner notification is required per the management agreement). -Estimate / work approval: No work proceeds unless you have personally approved it. If you didn't approve it, it isn't approved. When to escalate: You're genuinely unsure; it's high-consequence or legally sensitive; or it's an emergency (flood, fire, gas leak, etc.). Always frame as Yes/No or A/B/C with photos, estimate, WO #, and context. -When NOT to escalate: A resident is simply anxious or frustrated, or you can resolve it yourself within your authority. AI PROFICIENCY — HARD REQUIREMENT This is not a nice-to-have. Every member of our team uses AI daily, and you will be evaluated on your ability to use AI to work faster and produce higher-quality output. -Proficient with ChatGPT or Claude for drafting resident, owner, and vendor communications, summarizing, and problem-solving. -Able to write effective prompts that produce usable first drafts. -Comfortable using AI to research unfamiliar repair or maintenance situations and synthesize next steps. -Willing to adopt new AI tools and workflows without hand-holding. -You will be tested on this in the interview. If you have never used AI tools in a work context, please do not apply. REQUIREMENTS Must Have -Direct maintenance-coordination experience in US residential property management — not general admin or VA work. You have owned work orders end-to-end. -Hands-on AppFolio experience (work orders, reporting, owner and resident records). -Strong working knowledge of residential maintenance — HVAC, plumbing, electrical, appliances, and general repairs — including common repair timelines and vendor negotiation. -Excellent written and spoken English; professional, clear, and calm under pressure with residents, owners, and vendors. -Strong judgment and ownership — you make decisions within guardrails rather than waiting to be told. -Meticulous attention to detail and follow-through; you do not drop work orders. -Demonstrated AI proficiency (ChatGPT, Claude, or equivalent) in a real work context. -Reliable high-speed internet and a quiet, professional home-office setup. -Available Monday–Friday, US Central business hours. -Able to read a residential lease and apply it to real maintenance situations — determining responsibility, obligations, and authority from the lease terms. This is foundational to the role; you will rely on it daily. Nice to Have -3+ years of property management maintenance coordination experience. -Experience creating and improving maintenance processes, workflows, and SOPs. -Familiarity with HelpScout, Basecamp, and Google Workspace. -Knowledge of Texas habitability and repair-timeline standards. -Light automation experience (Zapier / Make) or genuine interest in building systems. We Will Not Move Forward With Candidates Who -Lack genuine, specific maintenance-coordination experience (general VA experience alone is not enough; please do not apply if you do not have prior experience in maintenance coordination in a property management company). -Cannot demonstrate practical lease comprehension — i.e., reading a lease and correctly determining maintenance responsibility and authority. -Have no demonstrated experience using AI tools at work. -Require constant direction — this role demands independent judgment within defined limits. -Cannot communicate clearly and professionally in English, or cannot commit to consistent Central-time hours. WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE The person who thrives in this role: -Takes ownership rather than passing problems to others. -Solves problems before escalating them. -Makes sound decisions with limited supervision. -Holds vendors accountable to scope, price, and quality. -Improves systems and processes proactively. -Communicates clearly and professionally. -Creates confidence among owners, residents, and leadership. OUR CORE VALUES -Extreme Ownership · Solutions, Not Excuses · Attention to Detail · Continuous Improvement · Professional Communication · -Accountability · Team-First Mentality TOOLS YOU WILL USE -AppFolio (property management / work orders) -HelpScout (SOP wikis & documentation) -Basecamp (project & task coordination) -Google Workspace (email , docs, sheets, drive) -ChatGPT / Claude (AI-assisted drafting & research) -A weather app set to Austin, TX (for weather-sensitive repair prioritization) SCHEDULE -Full-time (~40 hrs/week), Monday–Friday, 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM Central. -This is a weekday role — no weekend work. Weekend and after-hours emergency coverage is handled by a separate tea ---------- mber; you are responsible for a clean Friday handoff of any open or pending items. -Remote — Philippines-based candidates only. -First 90 days are a trial period; either party may end the engagement with 7 days' written notice. Compensation reviewed at 90 days and annually thereafter. HIRING PROCESS -Apply — Submit your resume and complete the TestGorilla assessments (link below). title: Experienced Lead Manager (Real Estate)
description: We are hiring a Lead Manager to nurture and manage our pipeline of real estate leads, ensuring no opportunities slip through the cracks. As a Lead Manager, you will be the main point of contact for warm leads: following up with prospects, building rapport, and guiding them until they are ready to close or speak with our acquisitions closer. Additionally, you will engage in targeted outbound prospecting, using our high-quality data (e.g. fresh county records for probate and foreclosures) to initiate conversations with potential sellers. This hybrid role is critical – you'll keep our funnel organized and full by both managing incoming leads and proactively hunting new ones. If you are a people-person who is also organized and driven, this could be a perfect fit. Who We Are: The OmniKey Group is founded and led by top-ranking Fortune 500 Sales Managers with a proven track record of developing and employing elite talent. We don't just build businesses — we build careers. As we scale aggressively, we are looking for driven individuals who want to grow alongside a leadership team that knows how to invest in people. Responsibilities: Lead Nurturing: Manage a pipeline of ~50 active leads in our CRM. Promptly follow up with interested home sellers via phone, text, and email . Your goal is to build relationships over time – check in regularly, understand their situation, and keep our company top-of-mind for when they're ready to sell. Initial Lead Qualification: Call new inquiries (from inbound calls or web forms) as soon as they come in. Have a friendly introductory conversation to gather information: Why might they sell? When? What's the property condition? Identify serious motivation versus casual interest. Ensure every new lead is contacted and categorized (hot, warm, long-term, etc.). Set Appointments: When a lead is qualified and shows strong interest/motivation, schedule an appointment or transfer the call to our acquisitions closer. You control the calendar for our acquisition team – scheduling consultations or property visits. Make sure our closer gets all key information before the meeting. Outbound Prospecting: Devote part of your time to reaching out to cold prospects from our premium data lists (such as probate, pre-foreclosure, or other niche lists we've pulled). Use cold calling or personalized texts/emails to introduce our service and see if they have a property they might consider selling. This "deep prospecting" uses the valuable data provided by our Data Manager to generate new leads beyond the ones who come to us. Pipeline Organization: Keep the CRM updated meticulously. Log every call, update lead statuses, and add detailed notes after each contact. Set follow-up reminders for each lead so you always remember to call back when promised. No lead should ever be forgotten or left without a next action. Team Coordination: Work closely with the acquisitions (closing) team. Clearly hand off highly motivated leads with full context (notes about the seller's situation, motivation level, etc.). After our closer makes an offer, circle back with the seller to address any concerns or continue nurturing if they didn't sign immediately. Essentially, you bridge the gap between initial interest and closed deal, keeping communication smooth. Requirements: Excellent Communication: Fluent English speaker who can converse naturally and confidently with U.S. homeowners. You have a friendly phone demeanor, active listening skills, and can build trust over multiple conversations. (Experience talking to older American homeowners is a plus – you can strike the right tone of patience and professionalism.) Sales/Customer Service Experience: 1+ year in a role like sales representative, account manager, customer service, or any position requiring consistent client follow-up. Real estate experience (especially in investing or related to motivated sellers) is highly advantageous – if you've dealt with sellers or real estate leads before, let us know! Follow-Up and Organizational Skills: A proven ability to juggle dozens of leads and keep an organized system. You never let a task or callback slip. Using a CRM or lead management system should be second nature to you. (If you pride yourself on color-coded spreadsheets or meticulous task lists, that's a good sign!)Google Drive Persuasion & Empathy: You know how to connect with people, ask the right questions, and handle objections. You're empathetic to sellers' situations (many may be in tough circumstances like foreclosure, probate, etc.) and also persuasive in highlighting how our service can help them. Tech-Savvy: Comfortable with CRM software, click-to-call phone systems, and general productivity tools (Google Workspace, etc.). Able to learn new apps quickly. Also, must have reliable internet and a headset/quiet workspace for frequent calls. Work Hours: Available to work full-time on US hours (e.g. 9am–6pm PST). Leads must be called quickly during da ---------- hours in the US. Flexibility to occasionally adjust hours for an urgent lead is appreciated. We are seeking someone who can commit long-term (12+ months) and become an integral part of the team. What We Offer: Base Pay + Commission: Competitive base salary plus commission on each deal you help close. Your earning potential grows with every deal. Impactful Work: This role is at the heart of our business – you will directly influence our revenue by turning leads into deals. It's rewarding to see your relationship-building result in a family helped and a successful transaction. We often deal with homeowners in difficult situations; you'll take pride in guiding them toward a solution. Training & Development: We will provide training on our scripts, CRM, and the real estate investment process. You'll learn about the wholesale home-buying industry, negotiations, and how to evaluate seller motivation. Ongoing coaching will be available to sharpen your skills (we succeed when you succeed). Team Environment: Work with a supportive, growth-minded team. We maintain open communication and regular team check-ins despite being remote. You'll get feedback and recognition for your hard work. We also encourage new ideas – if you have suggestions to improve our follow-up processes, we want to hear them. Remote Work Lifestyle: This is a 100% remote position. Save on commute time and work from the comfort of your home (or home office). As long as you can reliably cover the required hours and stay connected, you'll enjoy the flexibility of remote work. How to Apply: If you're excited about nurturing leads and driving deals, we'd love to hear from you. Please send your resume and a short voice recording introducing yourself. In your intro, tell us why you're interested in this Lead Manager role and highlight any relevant experience (especially in real estate or sales). You can use a service like Vocaroo for the recording and share the link. Feel free to also include a brief note or cover letter about a time you successfully convinced a customer or closed a tough deal – we value those who take initiative to showcase their skills. Qualified candidates will be invited to a Zoom interview (and possibly a role-play exercise). Come join a team where your follow-up prowess will be highly valued and rewarded!

title: Customer Service Support Representative

Tell us in a few sentences about your customer support experience, especially any ecommerce or email support work. Apply today and we will be in touch.

job_title: B2B Cold Caller / Appointment Setter for U.S. Local Businesses
description: # B2B Cold Caller / Appointment Setter for U.S. Local Businesses ## Job Overview We are hiring a B2B cold caller / appointment setter to call local businesses in the United States and book qualified appointments with business owners. We work with plumbing and home service businesses. Our service helps these businesses capture missed and after-hours calls so they can book more jobs instead of losing leads to voi cemail or slow follow-up. Your job is to call business owners, ask simple qualification questions, and book appointments for our closer. You are not responsible for closing the sale. Your job is to set quality appointments with interested business owners. ## Compensation This role includes guaranteed hourly pay plus performance bonuses. Paid trial: **$3 USD per hour for the first 10 hours** After successful trial: **$4 USD per hour** Performance bonuses: **$12.5 USD for every qualified appointment that shows up** **$50 USD for every appointment that becomes a closed, paid client** A closed, paid client means the business owner attends the appointment, signs the agreement, and pays the first invoice. Bonuses are paid after the appointment shows or after the client’s first payment is received. ## Daily Call Expectations Expected ramp-up: **Training period:** 75–100 dials per day **Week 1:** 100–150 dials per day **Week 2:** 150–200 dials per day **Experienced target:** 200–300 dials per day depending on shift length and call quality All calls must be made through our CRM/calling system so activity can be tracked. Calls made outside the CRM will not count. ## Main Performance Goal The main goal is to book qualified appointments with business owners. A realistic target is: **3–5 qualified appointments per week once fully trained** Quality matters more than fake volume. We do not want random appointments with people who are not decision makers. ## What Counts as a Qualified Appointment An appointment counts as qualified only if: * You spoke with the owner or decision maker * The business is a plumbing company or relevant home service business * The owner is interested in missed-call or after-hours call capture * The owner understands why the meeting is being booked * The appointment is added to the calendar * The owner receives a confirmation message * CRM notes are fully completed * The prospect is not fake, spam, or unable to make decisions A random “call me later” does not count as a qualified appointment. ## Responsibilities You will be responsible for: * Making outbound calls to U.S. local businesses * Asking for the owner or decision maker * Following the provided script * Asking about missed calls, after-hours calls, voi cemail , and answering services * Finding out if the business has a problem with missed calls or slow follow-up * Booking qualified appointments on the calendar * Sending appointment confirmation messages * Taking clear notes in the CRM * Updating lead status after every call * Creating follow-up tasks for interested prospects * Sending a daily activity report ## Example Call Script You will be trained on a script like this: “Hey, is this {{Business Name}}?” “Awesome, is the owner around?” When speaking with the owner: “Hey {{Owner Name}}, this is {{Your Name}}. Quick question — when someone calls after-hours for an emergency plumbing job, does that go to a live person, voi cemail , or an answering service?” If they answer: “Got it. The reason I’m calling is we help plumbing companies capture missed and after-hours calls so they can turn more of those calls into booked jobs instead of losing them to voi cemail . Would it be crazy to have Maxx take 15 minutes to show you how it works?” If they already use an answering service: “That makes sense. Are they actually booking jobs into your calendar, or mostly just taking messages?” If interested: “Perfect. Maxx can show you how the missed-call revenue system works. Does tomorrow at {{time}} or {{time}} work better?” ## Required CRM Notes For every real conversation, you must enter notes in the CRM. Notes must include: * Business name * Owner or decision maker name * Phone number * Current call handling process * Whether they miss calls * What happens after-hours * Whether they use voi cemail , office staff, or answering service * Pain points mentioned * Interest level * Appointment date and time * Confirmation status * Objections or special notes If there are no notes, the appointment may not count. ## Required Skills You must have: * Strong spoken English * Confident phone voice * Cold calling experience * Ability to handle rejection * Ability to follow a script * Good note-taking skills * Reliable internet * Quiet work environment * Headset or clear microphone * Ability to work during U.S. business hours * Fast response time * Strong work ethic * Ability to make consistent outbound calls ## Preferred Experience Preferred but not required: * B2B cold calling experience * Appointment setting experience * Experience calling local businesses * Experience with GoHighLevel, Close, HubSpot, Salesforce, or other CRMs * Experience selling marketing, software, lead generation, or appointment setting services * Experience calling home service businesses ## Work Schedule You must be available to call during U.S. business hours. Preferred calling windows: Monday through Friday 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM U.S. time zones You may be calling businesses in Eastern, Central, Mountain, and Pacific time zones. ## Tracking and Accountability All calls must be tracked inside our CRM. We track: * Dials * Conversations * Decision makers reached * Follow-ups created * Qualified appointments booked * Appointments confirmed * Appointments that show * Closed clients If calls are not logged in the CRM, they do not count. ## Daily Report At the end of each workday, you must send a daily report with: * Total dials * Total conversations * Decision makers reached * Follow-ups created * Appointments booked * Appointments confirmed * Best lead notes * Main objections heard * Any issues or questions ## Application Instructions To apply, please send: 1. A 60-second voice recording introducing yourself 2. Your cold calling experience 3. Your appointment setting experience 4. Your available work schedule in U.S. time zones 5. Your internet speed screenshot 6. Your headset/microphone setup 7. The most outbound calls you have made in one day 8. A short answer to this question: “What would you say if a plumbing business owner says, ‘We already have someone answering calls’?” ## Test Script Please record yourself saying this: “Hey, is this {{Business Name}}? Awesome, is the owner around?” Then: “Hey {{Owner Name}}, this is {{Your Name}}. Quick question — when someone calls after-hours for an emergency plumbing job, does that go to a live person, voi cemail , or an answering service?” ## Final Note We are looking for someone reliable, coachable, and consistent. This role includes hourly pay and performance bonuses. If you can make calls, follow the script, book quality appointments, and keep accurate CRM notes, there is a strong opportunity to grow with us.

If you've been bouncing between small gigs and you're ready to settle into a single role where your work actually adds up over time and you get handed more as you earn it, this could be a good home. Here's roughly how a day goes. You open your accounts and get the day's content out, reels, feed posts, and stories, each one matching the voice of the account it belongs to. You spend real time in the comments and DMs, keeping things warm and human. You keep half an eye on what's working for similar accounts and what's trending, then fold the good ideas into what's coming up. When a clip needs a quick trim or a cleaner cover, you sort it yourself in CapCut or Canva. At the end of the day you log what went out and how it performed in a shared Google Sheet, so we always have a clear read on every account. The quiet skill underneath all of it is keeping each account's style, schedule, and rules cleanly separate, so nothing ever bleeds from one into another. This suits someone who genuinely likes order, gets a kick out of watching accounts grow off the back of steady daily effort, and would rather own one thing properly than juggle five things loosely. If you need someone checking in to keep you on task, or you want something light on the side, you'll be happier elsewhere, and that's fine. To do this well, a few things aren't optional. You'll need a proper computer that can handle media work, not a phone or tablet. You'll need internet that's fast and stable, with some kind of backup for when the power or connection drops. Your written English has to be strong, since you're writing captions and talking to people all day. You'll need to be around most days, weekends included, because the accounts don't take days off. And you'll need to genuinely manage yourself. We won't be standing over your shoulder, and we don't want to. What would put you near the top of the pile: real experience running several Instagram accounts at once. If you've handled ten or more, say so. Comfort in Google Sheets past the basics helps too, formulas, pivot tables, that kind of thing. What you get in return: a steady long-term role instead of another short-lived gig, pay that reflects what you actually bring, and the chance to grow into more responsibility as you prove yourself, including a say in how the work gets done as things expand. You'd also be working with us directly, not lost under layers of management. On how we hire: not off a polished resume and a hopeful note. There's a detailed application first, then a short paid trial on real accounts before any offer goes out. You're paid for that trial, because watching the real work is the only honest way for us to judge, and the only fair way for you to show what you can do. description: I am looking for a skilled Graphic Designer / Virtual Assistant to help with artwork preparation for a custom printing and apparel business. Main Responsibilities You will help with tasks such as: Redrawing low-quality logos into clean vector files Manually tracing artwork in Adobe Illustrator Converting raster images into vector files when possible Cleaning up blurry, pixelated, or low-resolution artwork Removing backgrounds and preparing transparent PNG files Preparing print-ready files for DTF transfers and apparel printing Creating t-shirt designs from ideas, references, or client concepts Creating simple logo concepts and brand graphics Sizing artwork correctly for shirts, hoodies, bags, and other products Creating mockups to show clients how designs may look on apparel Organizing design files clearly in Google Drive or another file system Making revisions based on feedback Required Skills Please apply only if you are comfortable with: Adobe Illustrator Adobe Photoshop Manual vector tracing Logo redraws Raster image cleanup Transparent PNG files Print-ready file setup Typography and layout design Apparel/t-shirt design Following instructions carefully Communicating clearly and asking questions when needed Important Please put the word DTF as the very first word at the top of your application so I know you read this section carefully. Bonus Skills These are not required, but they are a big plus: DTF printing experience Screen printing file preparation Color separations Spot colors Halftones Pantone color matching Gang sheet layout Canva Figma Procreate CorelDRAW Experience working with print shops, apparel brands, or promotional products The Type of Designer I’m Looking For I am not only looking for someone who can make things look nice. I need someone who understands clean artwork and print production. For example, if a client sends a small blurry logo, I need you to know whether it can be cleaned up, needs to be manually redrawn, or needs to be recreated from scratch. I am looking for someone who can take a rough idea and turn it into something professional, clean, and usable for printing. You should be able to understand things like: “This image is too low-quality, but I can redraw it.” “This file is okay for a mockup, but not good enough for printing.” “This design needs cleaner edges before we print it.” “I can make this into a transparent PNG and vector file.” “This logo has too many colors for screen print unless we simplify it.” “This design may need halftones, spot colors, or separations depending on the print method.” Examples of Work You May Be Given A client sends a screenshot of a logo and wants it on a shirt A business has a rough logo idea and needs a clean version A customer sends a photo and wants text added around it A design needs to be cleaned up for DTF printing A t-shirt idea needs to be created from a description A low-resolution PNG needs to be rebuilt as a vector file A design needs to be mocked up on a shirt A file needs to be prepared at the correct size with a transparent background A design may need simplified colors for screen printing Application Requirements When applying, please include: Your experience with Adobe Illustrator and Photoshop Examples of logo redraws or vector tracing work Examples of t-shirt or apparel designs you have made Before-and-after examples if you have them Any experience you have with DTF, screen printing, or print shops Any experience with halftones, spot colors, or color separations What file formats you can provide, such as AI, SVG, EPS, PDF, PNG, PSD, etc. Your expected hourly rate or monthly rate Your availability and preferred work schedule A short explanation of how you would handle a blurry low-resolution logo that a client wants printed on a shirt Please do not only send Canva designs. description: Type: Full-time or Part-time (start ~30 hrs/week, can grow) Schedule: US business/evening hours — this is a night shift in PH time Pay: Competitive base (USD) + uncapped per-appointment and per-deal bonuses Location: Remote (Philippines), work-from-home Read this whole post carefully — we only want the top 1% of callers, and the application instructions at the bottom will filter out everyone who didn't. We're a US real estate acquisitions company that buys houses for cash nationwide. We run high-volume outbound calling every day, and the phone is what d ---------- whether our closers get fed or the pipeline goes dry. We're not looking for someone to just "make dials." We're looking for a phone operator who understands that the cold caller is the closer's most important teammate. Our closers have done over half a billion dollars in sales over the phone. Your job is to put motivated home sellers in front of them. We measure everything. Callers who book appointments that show up and close get more leads, better lists, and more money. Callers who just ring dead air and clock out get cut. The setters we love treat every conversation like a live deal and every objection like a door, not a wall. THE ROLE You'll own the top of the funnel for our acquisitions team — calling skip-traced seller data, getting homeowners talking, uncovering real motivation, and locking qualified appointments our closers can turn into contracts. Three pillars to this role: 1. Conversations. You can stay sharp on call 300 like you were on call 3. Rejection doesn't rattle you, volume doesn't burn you out, and you genuinely enjoy talking to strangers — because you're good at it. 2. Discovery & rapport. Anyone can read a script. You get sellers to actually open up — why they're really selling, the situation behind it, the timeline, the number in their head. You listen more than you talk and you hear what they're not saying. 3. Setting. You don't just "generate interest" — you lock the appointment. You qualify hard (motivation, equity, timeline, condition), handle the objection before it lands, and set appointments that actually show up and close. A no-show is a loss, and you know it. The callers who win can do all three: grind the dials, build trust fast, and close for the next step. WHAT YOU'LL ACTUALLY BE DOING - Running a power dialer through skip-traced seller lists — measured on contacts and appointments set, not vanity dial counts - Holding real conversations with US homeowners and uncovering motivation, timeline, condition, and price expectations - Qualifying leads against our buy box — knowing a real motivated seller from a tire-kicker - Setting qualified appointments directly onto our closers' calendars - Handling objections and gatekeepers calmly ("I'm not interested," "what's your offer," "how'd you get my number") - Logging every single call accurately in the CRM — if it's not logged right, it didn't happen - Working callbacks fast — a seller who calls back is the hottest lead you'll get - Hitting daily targets across set call windows (we manage to dials/hr, contacts/hr, and appointments set) - Communicating with the team on Slack about what's landing and what's not WHAT WE NEED FROM YOU Phone skills: - 2+ years of high-volume outbound — US real estate acquisitions/wholesaling strongly preferred, or hard B2C cold calling that actually converted - Rejection-proof and high-energy through a full shift — call 300 sounds like call 3 - Excellent, clear, easy-to-understand spoken English — you're talking to US homeowners all day and they need to trust you instantly - You sound like a human having a conversation, not someone reading a script Sales & discovery: - You build rapport in the first 15 seconds and get past the wall - Real objection-handling — a calm, practiced answer to every common "no," and you know a real objection from a brush-off - Motivation discovery — you dig for the why behind the sale and the true timeline and number - Disciplined qualifying — you don't waste a closer's calendar on a weak lead, and you don't kill a strong one with a bad set Setup & process (non-negotiable): - Noise-canceling headset, a quiet home office, and reliable high-speed internet with a backup connection - Backup power (UPS/generator) — brownouts can't take you offline mid-shift - Comfortable on a power/predictive dialer (BatchDialer, Mojo, CallTools, or similar) - CRM discipline — you disposition every call, accurately, in real time - Self-directed and coachable — we give you the script, the data, and the windows; you bring the effort and the reps - Able to work US hours (night shift in the Philippines) consistently BONUS POINTS - US real estate acquisitions, wholesaling, or dispo experience - You've set appointments for high-ticket closers and understand the hand-off - You can listen back to a call and explain exactly why it went sideways and how you'd run it again - You study the craft — you steal from the best closers you know PAY & GROWTH - Base (USD) + uncapped bonuses per appointment set and per deal closed — your income scales with your results - Start ~30 hrs/week, with a clear path to full-time and more responsibility for top performers - We cover the dialer, the data/lists, the CRM, the scripts, and ongoing coaching HOW TO APPLY (read carefully — we skip incomplete applications) Start your application with the word "MOTIVATED" at the very top so we know you actually read this. Applications without it get deleted. Then send us: 1. A call recording — a real cold call or a realistic mock call, 2–5 minutes. This is the most important thing. Be honest about where you are. 3. One appointment or deal you're proud of — 3–4 sentences on the situation and why you locked it. 4. How you'd respond to "I'm not interested" (or "just send me a cash offer") — write it exactly the way you'd say it on the phone. 5. Your setup — internet speed (run a speed test), backup internet/power, headset, dialer experience, and your work environment. 6. Your expected rate — base hourly + what you'd want per appointment set and per deal closed. 7. Availability — hours per week and the earliest you can start (confirm you can work US night-shift hours).

description: We're a performance marketing agency running paid social for DTC brands across supplements, beauty, real estate, and lifestyle verticals. We spend serious money on Meta every month and creative is the lever that d ---------- whether accounts scale or stall. We're not looking for someone to just "cut videos" — we're looking for a creative partner who understands that on Meta, the editor is the media buyer's most important teammate. We test creative aggressively. Winners get scaled, losers get killed, and we iterate weekly. The editors we love are the ones who treat every ad like a hypothesis and every variant like a data point. THE ROLE You'll own the post-production pipeline for multiple brands. That means taking raw UGC footage, creator deliverables, product shots, sourced B-roll, and AI-generated assets and turning them into ad variants that print money on Meta. Three pillars to this role: 1. Editing. You can cut a UGC ad in your sleep — hooks, pacing, captions, sound design, the works. 2. Sourcing B-roll. A huge part of making UGC ads work is finding the right supporting footage. That means knowing where to pull stock clips, digging through Pinterest and TikTok for reference and inspiration, finding free-use clips on YouTube, scraping competitor ads fro ---------- ta ad library, and knowing which clips are licensed for commercial use vs. which will get us in trouble. Half the battle is taste — knowing the exact shot that lands the message — and the other half is research speed. 3. Generating B-roll and A-roll with AI. When sourced footage doesn't exist or doesn't fit, you generate it. If we need a shot of a woman pouring coffee at 6am with golden hour lighting and the sourced clips look generic, you should be able to generate that in Higgsfield or Flow inside an hour and have it cut into the edit by end of day. The editors who win in 2026 are the ones who can move fluidly between all three: cut creator UGC, source perfect supporting clips, and generate the impossible shots. That's what we're hiring for. WHAT YOU'LL ACTUALLY BE DOING - Editing 5–15 ad variants per week across multiple brands - Cutting hooks (we usually test 3–5 hook variants per concept, same body) - Pacing edits for direct response — fast cuts, motion, pattern interrupts, captioned throughout - Sourcing B-roll from stock libraries, social platforms, and free archives — and knowing what's legally clear to use - Building reference boards fro ---------- ta ad library, competitor ads, and viral organic content - Generating A-roll talking-head clips when we need spokesperson angles we don't have footage for - Creating AI B-roll: lifestyle shots, product close-ups, transformations, before/afters, environmental context - Building character-consistent AI footage when we're running a series or recurring "spokesperson" - Mixing UGC creator footage with sourced clips and AI-generated supplementary footage seamlessly - Adding captions (burned-in, branded styling), sound design, music, SFX - title: Senior Full-Stack Engineer (Next.js / E2B / Vercel Platforms)
job_title: Senior Full-Stack Engineer (Next.js / E2B / Vercel Platforms)
description: We're hiring a senior full-stack engineer to help us launch MythOS Pro, an AI-powered operating system for local service businesses (barbershops, salons, restaurants). It's a full platform: CRM, booking/calendar, payments, inventory, a workforce module, an AI agent (Mylo) that runs across all of it, and a website builder. You'll work directly with the founder and grow into a core engineering role as we get launch-ready. Strong English communication required. Priority #1 — Website Builder (the immediate need): Our builder lets a customer import their GitHub repo, edit their Next.js site inside our platform, then push to main, which triggers an automatic Vercel redeploy so their live site updates. We need this pipeline rock-solid: Fix reliability issues with our E2B sandbox (sandboxes sometimes fail to load / dev server doesn't bind correctly on port 3000). Reference: e2b-dev/fragments. Build a clean GitHub repo import flow: clone repo into the sandbox (sandbox.git.clone), npm install, boot the Next.js dev server, expose the preview URL into our editor iframe. Implement edit ? commit ? push-to-main back to the customer's GitHub repo via the GitHub App (installation token). Wire the push to trigger Vercel auto-redeploy, with each customer's site served on their own subdomain via Vercel for Platforms (multi-tenant). Help us finish setting this up. Sandbox lifecycle management: create, auto-pause on idle, resume on edit, kill on session end, with cost controls. Beyond the builder, there's a deep backlog across the whole platform — CRM, booking, payments integrations, inventory, the workforce module, and Mylo's agent capabilities. We want someone who can own significant pieces of the product and help drive us to launch. Our stack: Frontend/API surface (mythOS-pro): Next.js App Router, TypeScript, Supabase, Tailwind, deployed on Vercel. Agent runtime (mythos-claw): a custom Rust runtime that powers our Mylo agent — built on a fork of NEAR AI's IronClaw, blended with OpenClaw, Hermes, GoClaw, and other components. Runs as a long-running service on Google Cloud Run (Postgres/Neon, Redis/Upstash, embedded Hermes worker, Gemini integration). Other: GitHub App integration, E2B sandboxes, Vercel for Platforms (multi-tenant), Claude API, Pinecone vector search. The two runtimes communicate over HTTP — mythOS-pro is the public-facing surface, mythos-claw is the brain. Must have: Deep Next.js App Router + TypeScript experience and the ability to debug deployment/infra issues independently (Cloud Run, Vercel, sandboxed dev environments). Strong bonus / what sets you apart: Rust experience and comfort working in an agent runtime — we'd love someone who can contribute to mythos-claw itself, not just the Next.js surface.

description: About the Role •We are looking for a detail-oriented property researcher to help identify land parcels in the United States that may fit specific acquisition criteria. •This role requires strong web research skills, comfort using county GIS maps, attention to zoning and parcel details, and accurate Excel or Google Sheets work. •You  need to be reliable, organized, and able to follow detailed instructions. Primary Responsibilities •Research land parcels using LandID, county GIS maps, assessor records, property appraiser websites, zoning maps, planning department websites, and other public sources. (I will teach how to use LandID software if you have not used it). •Identify parcels that match specific search criteria such as acreage, zoning, road access, topography, wetlands, nearby development, utilities, and current listing status. •Enter parcel data into Excel or Google Sheets using a required format. •Record parcel number, owner name, owner mailing address, site address, acreage, zoning, land use, road access, nearby projects, notes, and source links. •Review GIS maps to check parcel boundaries, roads, nearby subdivisions, utilities, floodplain/wetland indicators, and surrounding development patterns. •Check whether a property appears to be currently listed for sale and exclude listed properties when instructed. •Organize findings clearly so another person can quickly verify the parcel. •Flag uncertain items instead of guessing. Required Skills •Strong Excel or Google Sheets skills, including sorting, filtering, formatting, hyperlinks, and clean data entry. •Ability to use online GIS maps and parcel viewers. •Ability to research zoning and land use information from county or city websites. •Strong attention to detail and accuracy. •Comfort working with U.S. property records and public data websites. •Ability to follow written instructions exactly. •Good written English for notes, summaries, and questions. •Reliable internet connection and ability to meet deadlines. Helpful Experience •Real estate research, land research, title research, GIS research, zoning research, or property data entry. •Experience with county assessor websites, planning and zoning maps, GIS parcel viewers, Google Earth, FEMA maps, or listing websites. •Experience researching agricultural land, development land, vacant land, or residential growth areas. •Experience checking roads, utilities, wetlands, floodplain, slope, and nearby residential development. Typical Parcel Criteria You May Research •20 or more acres. •Relatively flat land or limited topographical change. •At least two possible road access points when available. •No major wetlands on the usable portion of the property. •Agricultural, rural residential, transition, or similar zoning. •Near existing development or active residential building projects. •Near water, sewer, or other utility infrastructure when possible. •Not currently listed for sale, unless instructed otherwise. •Owner mailing address available from public records when possible. Work Product Expected •A clean Excel or Google Sheets file with one parcel per row. •Boundary marking for each parcel inside LandID software •Clear flags for anything uncertain or needing review. •Screenshots or map links when requested. Quality Standards •Accuracy matters more than speed. •Do not guess. Mark uncertain information as uncertain. •Keep spreadsheet formatting clean and consistent. •Do not include parcels that clearly fail the criteria. •Ask questions early if instructions are unclear.
