title: Operations & Project Manager (Fast Growing)
description: Operations Manager-Execution Partner-Project Killer-Fast-Growing Comic Book Company Own the operations backbone of a niche comic book brand, work directly with leadership, and get promoted fairly by numbers. This role is for that special person who wants to become truly exceptional. If that’s you, you already know this message is your signal. What You Get If You Win Here - High autonomy: once you’re ramped, you own your queue, schedule, and methods as long as the KPIs are hit. Lots of freedom to figure it out, great for someone that loves building with Legos - Direct proximity to leadership: you work daily with the Ops Manager on the most important projects in the company. - Clear advancement path: your growth is tied to visible numbers (tasks shipped, zero-miss cadence, freed founder/ops time, profit/leading metrics), not politics. - Insane skill growth: the pace and standards here mean every 12 months with us will feel like 3 years of experience in a normal VA/ops role. You can leapfrog your friends. If you join this will change your life. You will work harder than you’ve ever worked before and grow faster than you’ve ever grown before. - Comic Books!: you’re not just pushing random SaaS tickets; you’re inside a real comic book store seeing rare old comic books, private deals, and the business behind the Hollywood Marvel Movies that everyone loves! If you’re that person who enjoys working really hard to the point that it takes 2-3 people to do what you did listen up: Our tasks in asana for projects and ongoing operations are moving at a snail’s pace. Ops Manager + CEO is chasing tasks, slack policing, cleaning up Asana, and re-explaining context instead of focusing on their jobs. We’ve had “pleasant” VAs who: Can’t drive tasks to completion independently Mark tasks complete with no proof Miss reports/skip cadence and require chasing. Drift on ownership, urgency & follow thru Need hand-holding I don’t need another task hopper. I need a project killer who comes into ambiguity, creates structure, drives tasks to completion, and actually frees the Ops Manager to focus on his key projects. If this works, his deep work hours and project output go up because you’re handling everything else. We will measure that and tie your promotions/raises to it. This is not for everyone. We’re looking for winners. What You’ll Actually Do You will be Ops Manager’s execution partner and force-multiplier. Concrete outputs: Own Asana: every task has an owner, due date, Done Check, and proof link when completed Maintain an active queue of 20+ meaningful tasks, prioritized against our key rocks (Marketing, Sales, Ongoing Operations, Cleanup, Admin) Ship 25+ tasks/week with proof, minimal rework, and zero “ghosted” items Proactively handle operational issues/fires in designated lanes Maintain Reporting at Set Cadence, Follow-up loops across projects Add leverage: plug AI into our workflows (Asana, docs, reports) to make us faster and cleaner without being asked We do NOT need more SOPS-although you might tighten them on the fly. We need someone to do the operations. If you want to sit and write playbooks all day, this is the wrong seat-that will be an earned responsibility later. If you aren’t ready to work hard daily do not apply. How We Set You Up To Win (First 90 Days) We don’t just throw you in the deep end. In your first 30 days, you’ll shadow the Ops Manager, learn our Asana + reporting systems, and get a clear scorecard so you always know what “great” looks like. By 30 days, you’ll own your own project lanes with weekly 1:1s for feedback, support, and removing blockers so you can move faster instead of guessing what we want. Real Growth Example One of our Filipino teammates started with us on basic execution work at ~$800/month. Over time, he took ownership of his queue, fixed broken processes, and became the person we trusted to “just handle it.” As his scope grew, so did his comp and stability. Now he makes ~$2,500/month (and we’re working on getting him even more) because he stuck with it and actually grew. A lot of people say they want that, but their resumes show 6–12 month hops. The pattern here is simple: prove you can own outcomes over time, and we grow your responsibilities, trust, and pay accordingly. Schedule, Hours & Time Zone (No Surprises) This is a full time, US hours role (roughly US Eastern business hours) with a true 50–60 hour workweek during this growth season. Expect most weeks to be closer to that 60 hour mark. If you want a strict 40 hour cap, this is the wrong seat; if you want a place where extra effort is noticed, measured, and rewarded, you’ll feel at home here. This is not just a job. This is a commitment. What Winning Looks Like By Day 30: Ops Manager is spending ~95% of his time on projects, not Slack/Asana/admin fires, because you’re handling those and executing projects alongside him. Profit and leading metrics are moving up faster because of you By 12 months: You are Ops Manager’s go to operator & on track to become Ops Manager. Nothing important moves in Ops without you knowing. You own the Asana board, key ops projects, and reporting cadence. You’re the person we trust to “just handle it,” and your comp reflects that increased ownership. If you become that go to operator, you’ll have real say in how we run Ops – you won’t just be ‘executing tickets,’ you’ll help design the system.” Who This Is NOT For You prefer to ‘coordinate’ and assign tasks to others instead of doing the work yourself with excellence. You want to manage people before you’ve truly proven you can personally execute at a high level. You want a chill, low-pressure 9–5 You need to be told what to do all day and hate being judged by objective numbers You mark tasks complete without proof or next steps You change jobs every 6–18 months and blame the company/manager/market/ You get defensive or freeze when given direct feedback or pressure You are currently juggling multiple full time clients and want to “squeeze us in” on the side. You are mass applying to dozens of jobs and just want to see who bites first. Who This IS For You’ve stayed 2–3+ years in at least one role and can prove outcomes You like pressure, highly competitive environments, being the one who “gets it done” when others stall You’ve built systems (trackers, automations, SOPs), not just followed them You are tech-comfortable: Asana (or similar), CRMs, zaps, AI tools, simple web/ops/marketing stacks You’re willing to bet on one company instead of juggling lots of smaller, easier gigs. You hate corporate BS– endless meetings, vague goals, and politics – and would rather be rewarded for what you actually create. You’re happy to grind 50–60 hours/week no issues. We’re in a BIG growth & push season. It will be like this for the next year and then we’ll see. Everyone wants to grow a lot, but it’s actually happening here. Comp & Growth (All of this is written into your contract.) Months 1–3: Ramp / Trial • $800/month base, guaranteed, while you learn our systems and we test fit. • No bonus in this phase. You’re paid to prove you can hit the KPI floors. Month 4+ – Performance Based Upside • Base stays at $800 until you’ve hit KPI floors for 2 straight months. After that, base increases to $900/month going forward. • On top of base, you can earn: $400 bonus in months where you hit 3 out of 4 KPIs (with Output as one of them). $1,000 bonus in months where you hit 4 out of 4 KPIs on the weekly scorecard. • In practice, that means: Solid performance months ~$1,200–$1,300/month Killer months (4/4 KPIs)~$1,800–$1,900/month All bonuses are 100% KPI based  (shipped outcomes, taking load off the Ops Manager, zero CEO/manager rescues, tight open loops) and 4/5 culture. Training & Growth Investment (on top of pay) We actively invest in making you a sharper teammate. Over time, we’ll put thousands of dollars into your development (courses, coaching, playbooks, and tools) that we choose together based on what will make you more effective in this seat. We also protect uninterrupted deep?work blocks for you every week (no rando ---------- etings, no Slack spam). You’re paid to ship outcomes, not sit in back?to?back Zoom calls. Important: This is an ON FIELD role. You will not have a team under you to delegate to. 95% of your time is doing the work yourself, 5% is light coordination. If your default mode is to make plans and pass tasks to others, this will be a bad fit. How To Apply (24-Hour Test) Our Hiring Process (So There Are No Surprises) If your 24 hour answers impress us, the next steps are: A short interview focused on your past execution. A live 60 minute work trial inside our real tools where you’ll work directly with the Ops Manager. We do this because talk is cheap. If you don’t like being tested on real work before getting hired, this won’t be a fit. Do NOT click quick-apply. In the next 24 hours, you must: Reply with answers to ALL of these (short but specific; bullets are fine): Q1: Describe the most complex project you personally drove fro ---------- ssy start to completion where you did most of the execution yourself, not just assigning tasks. Include at least one example of how you set your own deadlines and moved forward when other people were slow to respond.” Q2: Share 3 links or screenshots (Google Docs, Sheets, Asana boards, trackers, automations, etc.) that you built yourself which show how you organize and drive work. Briefly explain each. Q3: You have 30 tasks due this week and realize you’ll miss 5. Walk me through, step-by-step, how you handle it with your manager and stakeholders. Q4:  Below are 6 messy “tasks” we actually see (all dumped into one list): – “Fix Asana, it’s a mess” – “Seller lead texting follow up??” – “Finance com/projections cadence d2 ” – “Inventory backlog insane” – “Need better reporting” – “Update SOPs In this role you will NOT have anyone to delegate to assume it’s just you and the Ops Manager. In a Google Doc, please: Rewrite these into clear tasks with: Owner (you or Ops Manager), Due Date (next 7–30 days), and a concrete Done Check + proof required. “Write your task descriptions as if you are committing: ‘I will do X by Y time. If Z doesn’t happen by [time], here’s my fallback.’ Generic ‘follow up / request access’ answers will fail you.” Put them in the order you’d actually do them and explain why in 3–5 bullet points. Link the Google Doc here (view access). Spend no more than 30–45 minutes. If you can’t figure this out on your own, this role will be too hard in real life – that’s okay, just skip applying. Attach your PDF resume/Google Drive link. Compensation here is performance based. Raises are earned through clearly exceeding KPIs and demonstrating core values consistently. If you want “stability” to mean “I can coast and still get raises,” this won’t feel stable. If you want stability to mean “the better I get, the more valuable and secure I become,” you’ll like it here.

title: Financial Operations Manager
description: We’re Hiring: Financial Operations Manager We are looking for a highly organized, proactive, and detail-oriented Financial Operations Manager to support bookkeeping, reporting, payroll coordination, cash flow tracking, tax coordination, and operational financial analytics across multiple business and personal entities. This role is ideal for someone who is not just comfortable with numbers, but also systems-minded, AI-first, and able to help leadership stay financially organized across several moving parts. We need someone who can take ownership, think ahead, identify issues before they become problems, and use tools, systems, and AI to make financial operations cleaner and more efficient. You will work closely with leadership and coordinate with tax consultants, contractors, affiliates, and financial service providers. ## About the Role You will help manage financial operations across multiple entities, including personal finances, real estate-related businesses, and a growing SaaS company. This includes maintaining accurate records, preparing financial reports, tracking cash flow, coordinating tax documentation, monitoring contractor and affiliate payments, and supporting leadership with financial visibility and decision-making. This is not a passive bookkeeping role. We are looking for someone who can manage recurring responsibilities, improve financial systems, flag risks early, and recommend better ways to organize, report, and automate finance-related work. The role serves as the primary financial coordination point between ownership, tax professionals, contractors, affiliates, and financial service providers. ## What You’ll Do ### Bookkeeping & Financial Records * Maintain bookkeeping and financial records across multiple business and personal entities. * Keep transactions properly categorized and reconciled. * Ensure financial records are accurate, organized, and up to date. * Maintain clean documentation for expenses, income, transfers, contractor payments, affiliate payouts, and business obligations. * Identify inconsistencies, missing records, or unusual activity and flag them proactively. ### Financial Reporting & Cash Flow * Prepare monthly financial reports and cash flow updates. * Monitor cash balances across accounts and flag upcoming funding needs. * Advise ownership when transfers are needed to cover payroll, taxes, contractor payments, subscriptions, affiliate payouts, and other obligations. * Support forecasting and financial planning through clear reporting and analysis. * Help leadership understand what the numbers mean, not just what the numbers are. ### Tax Coordination & Compliance Support * Coordinate with tax consultants and assist with tax preparation. * Help organize tax documents, tax organizers, contractor records, and compliance-related files. * Monitor contractors and affiliates for payment tracking and 1099 compliance. * Ensure financial documentation is organized and accessible for tax professionals. * Track recurring tax-related deadlines and follow up before they become urgent. ### Payroll & Contractor Payments * Process or coordinate payroll for business ownership and tea ---------- mbers where applicable. * Track contractor and affiliate payouts. * Review payout approvals and ensure payment information is accurate. * Maintain records of completed and pending payments. * Help improve payment tracking systems so there is clear visibility into who has been paid, who is pending, and what requires approval. ### SaaS / Operational Analytics * Manage Stride CRM user sign-up databases and related financial tracking. * Monitor user analytics, affiliate performance, and payout approvals. * Help track revenue, churn, signups, affiliate activity, and related SaaS metrics. * Support leadership with insights that connect financial data to business performance. * Identify trends, gaps, or anomalies in business performance data. ### Process Improvement & AI Leverage * Use AI tools to reduce repetitive manual work and improve reporting speed. * Use AI to help organize financial data, summarize reports, analyze spreadsheets, create checklists, draft documentation, and identify process gaps. * Look for recurring finance tasks that can be automated, systemized, or simplified. * Document repeatable workflows so the finance function becomes easier to manage over time. * Help turn messy information into clean, usable trackers, reports, and decision-making tools. ### Financial Liaison & Communication * Serve as the primary financial coordination point between ownership, tax professionals, contractors, affiliates, and financial service providers. * Communicate clearly when information is missing, deadlines are approaching, or decisions are needed. * Help keep leadership informed without requiring constant follow-up. * Ask smart questions when something is unclear instead of guessing. ## What We’re Looking For ### Required * Strong bookkeeping and financial operations experience. * Experience preparing financial reports and cash flow updates. * Comfortable managing financial records across multiple entities or business units. * Strong attention to detail and accuracy. * Clear written communication. * Highly organized and reliable. * Able to work independently and follow through without constant supervision. * Comfortable handling sensitive financial information with discretion. * Willing to document processes and improve systems over time. * Proactive enough to flag risks, missing information, or upcoming obligations before being asked. * Comfortable using AI tools to improve speed, organization, documentation, reporting, and analysis. ### Strongly Preferred * Experience working with U.S.-based businesses. * Experience coordinating with tax preparers, accountants, or CPAs. * Familiarity with payroll, contractor payments, and 1099 tracking. * Experience supporting entrepreneurs, real estate businesses, SaaS companies, or multi-entity owners. * Experience with financial dashboards, spreadsheets, and operational reporting. * Strong Google Sheets or Excel skills. * Ability to use AI tools thoughtfully and responsibly in financial operations. ### Bonus Points * Experience with Xero, QuickBooks, Google Sheets, Stripe, payroll tools, or affiliate tracking. * Experience with real estate, land investing, or SaaS metrics. * CPA, accounting degree, bookkeeping certification, or tax-related experience. * Ability to build or improve financial dashboards. * Experience building SOPs or documentation for finance workflows. * Experience creating financial trackers, forecasting models, or automated reporting systems. ## Who You Are You are someone who: * Takes initiative instead of waiting to be chased. * Uses AI and automation to reduce repetitive manual work. * Thinks critically about financial systems, reporting, and process gaps. * Notices risks early and communicates them clearly. * Can turn messy information into organized reports, trackers, and next steps. * Looks for better ways to complete recurring finance tasks. * Understands that this role is not just bookkeeping, but financial operations support for leadership decision-making. * Protects sensitive information and handles financial data with care. * Is comfortable working in a fast-moving environment with multiple businesses and priorities. * Can balance accuracy, speed, and good judgment. ## Success in This Role In the first 30 days, success would look like understanding the financial structure, current reporting process, recurring obligations, payroll/payment cadence, and key entities involved. You should be able to identify what reports exist, what is missing, what needs cleanup, and what recurring workflows must be protected. By 60–90 days, we would expect you to own the recurring finance cadence more independently, provide clear monthly reports, flag cash flow needs ahead of time, maintain organized records, support tax coordination, and help improve overall financial visibility across the businesses. Long term, success means leadership has cleaner visibility into cash flow, reporting, taxes, contractor payments, affiliate payouts, and business performance without constantly having to chase information. ## Compensation & Details * Remote position * Part-time or full-time depending on experience and fit * Long-term opportunity for the right person * Compensation based on experience, skill level, and communication ability * Must be available for some overlap with U.S. Eastern Time * Reports directly to leadership ## How to Apply We’d love to get to know the person behind the resume, not just look through generic links or a basic application. Please apply here: ---------- In the form, we’ll ask for: 1. Your resume 2. A short summary of your bookkeeping / financial operations experience 3. Your expected hourly rate 4. A short Loom video For the Loom, please keep it around 2–4 minutes and answer: 1. Tell us about the most complex bookkeeping, financial operations, or multi-entity finance role you’ve handled. 2. How do you stay organized when managing finances across multiple entities, people, accounts, or deadlines? 3. What recurring finance tasks do you think should be automated or systemized? We personally review applications and videos because we’re looking for someone who brings more than bookkeeping experience. We’re looking for someone thoughtful, proactive, organized, and able to bring real financial clarity to the team.

This is NOT a traditional “make Canva posts and schedule content” role. We want someone who studies what’s working online, identifies repeatable content formats, translates trends into our brand voice, and helps build a content machine. You’ll work directly with founders and our production/editing team to create a pipeline of content ideas that can actually be filmed and executed. Your Mission Your job is to help us consistently create content that grows reach, builds authority, and drives business. You’ll research what’s performing, break it down into repeatable frameworks, organize content plans, and prepare everything our filming/editing team needs. Think: Trend Scout + Content Strategist + Creative Producer. Responsibilities 1. title: Operations & Project Execution (Fast Growing)
description: Operations Manager-Execution Partner-Project Killer-Fast-Growing Comic Book Company Own the operations backbone of a niche comic book brand, work directly with leadership, and get promoted fairly by numbers. This role is for that special person who wants to become truly exceptional. If that’s you, you already know this message is your signal. What You Get If You Win Here - High autonomy: once you’re ramped, you own your queue, schedule, and methods as long as the KPIs are hit. Lots of freedom to figure it out, great for someone that loves building with Legos - Direct proximity to leadership: you work daily with the Ops Manager on the most important projects in the company. - Clear advancement path: your growth is tied to visible numbers (tasks shipped, zero-miss cadence, freed founder/ops time, profit/leading metrics), not politics. - Insane skill growth: the pace and standards here mean every 12 months with us will feel like 3 years of experience in a normal VA/ops role. You can leapfrog your friends. If you join this will change your life. You will work harder than you’ve ever worked before and grow faster than you’ve ever grown before. - Comic Books!: you’re not just pushing random SaaS tickets; you’re inside a real comic book store seeing rare old comic books, private deals, and the business behind the Hollywood Marvel Movies that everyone loves! If you’re that person who enjoys working really hard to the point that it takes 2-3 people to do what you did listen up: Our tasks in asana for projects and ongoing operations are moving at a snail’s pace. Ops Manager + CEO is chasing tasks, slack policing, cleaning up Asana, and re-explaining context instead of focusing on their jobs. We’ve had “pleasant” VAs who: Can’t drive tasks to completion independently Mark tasks complete with no proof Miss reports/skip cadence and require chasing. Drift on ownership, urgency & follow thru Need hand-holding I don’t need another task hopper. I need a project killer who comes into ambiguity, creates structure, drives tasks to completion, and actually frees the Ops Manager to focus on his key projects. If this works, his deep work hours and project output go up because you’re handling everything else. We will measure that and tie your promotions/raises to it. This is not for everyone. We’re looking for winners. What You’ll Actually Do You will be Ops Manager’s execution partner and force-multiplier. Concrete outputs: Own Asana: every task has an owner, due date, Done Check, and proof link when completed Maintain an active queue of 20+ meaningful tasks, prioritized against our key rocks (Marketing, Sales, Ongoing Operations, Cleanup, Admin) Ship 25+ tasks/week with proof, minimal rework, and zero “ghosted” items Proactively handle operational issues/fires in designated lanes Maintain Reporting at Set Cadence, Follow-up loops across projects Add leverage: plug AI into our workflows (Asana, docs, reports) to make us faster and cleaner without being asked We do NOT need more SOPS-although you might tighten them on the fly. We need someone to do the operations. If you want to sit and write playbooks all day, this is the wrong seat-that will be an earned responsibility later. If you aren’t ready to work hard daily do not apply. How We Set You Up To Win (First 90 Days) We don’t just throw you in the deep end. In your first 30 days, you’ll shadow the Ops Manager, learn our Asana + reporting systems, and get a clear scorecard so you always know what “great” looks like. By 30 days, you’ll own your own project lanes with weekly 1:1s for feedback, support, and removing blockers so you can move faster instead of guessing what we want. Real Growth Example One of our Filipino teammates started with us on basic execution work at ~$800/month. Over time, he took ownership of his queue, fixed broken processes, and became the person we trusted to “just handle it.” As his scope grew, so did his comp and stability. Now he makes ~$2,500/month (and we’re working on getting him even more) because he stuck with it and actually grew. A lot of people say they want that, but their resumes show 6–12 month hops. The pattern here is simple: prove you can own outcomes over time, and we grow your responsibilities, trust, and pay accordingly. Schedule, Hours & Time Zone (No Surprises) This is a full time, US hours role (roughly US Eastern business hours) with a true 50–60 hour workweek during this growth season. Expect most weeks to be closer to that 60 hour mark. If you want a strict 40 hour cap, this is the wrong seat; if you want a place where extra effort is noticed, measured, and rewarded, you’ll feel at home here. This is not just a job. This is a commitment. What Winning Looks Like By Day 30: Ops Manager is spending ~95% of his time on projects, not Slack/Asana/admin fires, because you’re handling those and executing projects alongside him. Profit and leading metrics are moving up faster because of you By 12 months: You are Ops Manager’s go to operator & on track to become Ops Manager. Nothing important moves in Ops without you knowing. You own the Asana board, key ops projects, and reporting cadence. You’re the person we trust to “just handle it,” and your comp reflects that increased ownership. If you become that go to operator, you’ll have real say in how we run Ops – you won’t just be ‘executing tickets,’ you’ll help design the system.” Who This Is NOT For You prefer to ‘coordinate’ and assign tasks to others instead of doing the work yourself with excellence. You want to manage people before you’ve truly proven you can personally execute at a high level. You want a chill, low-pressure 9–5 You need to be told what to do all day and hate being judged by objective numbers You mark tasks complete without proof or next steps You change jobs every 6–18 months and blame the company/manager/market/ You get defensive or freeze when given direct feedback or pressure You are currently juggling multiple full time clients and want to “squeeze us in” on the side. You are mass applying to dozens of jobs and just want to see who bites first. Who This IS For You’ve stayed 2–3+ years in at least one role and can prove outcomes You like pressure, highly competitive environments, being the one who “gets it done” when others stall You’ve built systems (trackers, automations, SOPs), not just followed them You are tech-comfortable: Asana (or similar), CRMs, zaps, AI tools, simple web/ops/marketing stacks You’re willing to bet on one company instead of juggling lots of smaller, easier gigs. You hate corporate BS– endless meetings, vague goals, and politics – and would rather be rewarded for what you actually create. You’re happy to grind 50–60 hours/week no issues. We’re in a BIG growth & push season. It will be like this for the next year and then we’ll see. Everyone wants to grow a lot, but it’s actually happening here. Comp & Growth (All of this is written into your contract.) Months 1–3: Ramp / Trial • $800/month base, guaranteed, while you learn our systems and we test fit. • No bonus in this phase. You’re paid to prove you can hit the KPI floors. Month 4+ – Performance Based Upside • Base stays at $800 until you’ve hit KPI floors for 2 straight months. After that, base increases to $900/month going forward. • On top of base, you can earn: $400 bonus in months where you hit 3 out of 4 KPIs (with Output as one of them). $1,000 bonus in months where you hit 4 out of 4 KPIs on the weekly scorecard. • In practice, that means: Solid performance months ~$1,200–$1,300/month Killer months (4/4 KPIs)~$1,800–$1,900/month All bonuses are 100% KPI based  (shipped outcomes, taking load off the Ops Manager, zero CEO/manager rescues, tight open loops) and 4/5 culture. Training & Growth Investment (on top of pay) We actively invest in making you a sharper teammate. Over time, we’ll put thousands of dollars into your development (courses, coaching, playbooks, and tools) that we choose together based on what will make you more effective in this seat. We also protect uninterrupted deep work blocks for you every week (no rando ---------- etings, no Slack spam). You’re paid to ship outcomes, not sit in back to back Zoom calls. Important: This is an ON FIELD role. You will not have a team under you to delegate to. 95% of your time is doing the work yourself, 5% is light coordination. If your default mode is to make plans and pass tasks to others, this will be a bad fit. Compensation here is performance based. Raises are earned through clearly exceeding KPIs and demonstrating core values consistently. If you want “stability” to mean “I can coast and still get raises,” this won’t feel stable. If you want stability to mean “the better I get, the more valuable and secure I become,” you’ll like it here. How To Apply (24-Hour Test) Our Hiring Process (So There Are No Surprises) If your 24 hour answers impress us, the next steps are: A short interview focused on your past execution. A live 60 minute work trial inside our real tools where you’ll work directly with the Ops Manager. We do this because talk is cheap. If you don’t like being tested on real work before getting hired, this won’t be a fit. Do NOT click quick-apply. In the next 24 hours, you must: Reply with answers to ALL of these (short but specific; bullets are fine): Q1: Describe the most complex project you personally drove fro ---------- ssy start to completion where you did most of the execution yourself, not just assigning tasks. Include at least one example of how you set your own deadlines and moved forward when other people were slow to respond.” Q2: Share 3 links or screenshots (Google Docs, Sheets, Asana boards, trackers, automations, etc.) that you built yourself which show how you organize and drive work. Briefly explain each. Q3: You have 30 tasks due this week and realize you’ll miss 5. Walk me through, step-by-step, how you handle it with your manager and stakeholders. Q4:  Below are 6 messy “tasks” we actually see (all dumped into one list): – “Fix Asana, it’s a mess” – “Seller lead texting follow up??” – “Finance com/projections cadence d2 ” – “Inventory backlog insane” – “Need better reporting” – “Update SOPs In this role you will NOT have anyone to delegate to assume it’s just you and the Ops Manager. In a Google Doc, please: Rewrite these into clear tasks with: Owner (you or Ops Manager), Due Date (next 7–30 days), and a concrete Done Check + proof required. “Write your task descriptions as if you are committing: ‘I will do X by Y time. If Z doesn’t happen by [time], here’s my fallback.’ Generic ‘follow up / request access’ answers will fail you.” Put them in the order you’d actually do them and explain why in 3–5 bullet points. Link the Google Doc here (view access). Spend no more than 30–45 minutes. If you can’t figure this out on your own, this role will be too hard in real life – that’s okay, just skip applying. Attach your PDF resume/Google Drive link.

Lots of freedom to figure it out, great for someone that loves building with Legos - Direct proximity to leadership: you work daily with the Ops Manager on the most important projects in the company. - Clear advancement path: your growth is tied to visible numbers (tasks shipped, zero-miss cadence, freed founder/ops time, profit/leading metrics), not politics. - Insane skill growth: the pace and standards here mean every 12 months with us will feel like 3 years of experience in a normal VA/ops role. You can leapfrog your friends. If you join this will change your life. You will work harder than you’ve ever worked before and grow faster than you’ve ever grown before. - Comic Books!: you’re not just pushing random SaaS tickets; you’re inside a real comic book store seeing rare old comic books, private deals, and the business behind the Hollywood Marvel Movies that everyone loves! If you’re that person who enjoys working really hard to the point that it takes 2-3 people to do what you did listen up: Our tasks in asana for projects and ongoing operations are moving at a snail’s pace. Ops Manager + CEO is chasing tasks, slack policing, cleaning up Asana, and re-explaining context instead of focusing on their jobs. We’ve had “pleasant” VAs who: Can’t drive tasks to completion independently Mark tasks complete with no proof Miss reports/skip cadence and require chasing. Drift on ownership, urgency & follow thru Need hand-holding I don’t need another task hopper. I need a project killer who comes into ambiguity, creates structure, drives tasks to completion, and actually frees the Ops Manager to focus on his key projects. If this works, his deep work hours and project output go up because you’re handling everything else. We will measure that and tie your promotions/raises to it. This is not for everyone. We’re looking for winners. What You’ll Actually Do You will be Ops Manager’s execution partner and force-multiplier. Concrete outputs: Own Asana: every task has an owner, due date, Done Check, and proof link when completed Maintain an active queue of 20+ meaningful tasks, prioritized against our key rocks (Marketing, Sales, Ongoing Operations, Cleanup, Admin) Ship 25+ tasks/week with proof, minimal rework, and zero “ghosted” items Proactively handle operational issues/fires in designated lanes Maintain Reporting at Set Cadence, Follow-up loops across projects Add leverage: plug AI into our workflows (Asana, docs, reports) to make us faster and cleaner without being asked We do NOT need more SOPS-although you might tighten them on the fly. We need someone to do the operations. If you want to sit and write playbooks all day, this is the wrong seat-that will be an earned responsibility later. If you aren’t ready to work hard daily do not apply. How We Set You Up To Win (First 90 Days) We don’t just throw you in the deep end. In your first 30 days, you’ll shadow the Ops Manager, learn our Asana + reporting systems, and get a clear scorecard so you always know what “great” looks like. By 30 days, you’ll own your own project lanes with weekly 1:1s for feedback, support, and removing blockers so you can move faster instead of guessing what we want. Real Growth Example One of our Filipino teammates started with us on basic execution work at ~$800/month. Over time, he took ownership of his queue, fixed broken processes, and became the person we trusted to “just handle it.” As his scope grew, so did his comp and stability. Now he makes ~$2,500/month (and we’re working on getting him even more) because he stuck with it and actually grew. A lot of people say they want that, but their resumes show 6–12 month hops. The pattern here is simple: prove you can own outcomes over time, and we grow your responsibilities, trust, and pay accordingly. Schedule, Hours & Time Zone (No Surprises) This is a full time, US hours role (roughly US Eastern business hours) with a true 50–60 hour workweek during this growth season. Expect most weeks to be closer to that 60 hour mark. If you want a strict 40 hour cap, this is the wrong seat; if you want a place where extra effort is noticed, measured, and rewarded, you’ll feel at home here. This is not just a job. This is a commitment. What Winning Looks Like By Day 30: Ops Manager is spending ~95% of his time on projects, not Slack/Asana/admin fires, because you’re handling those and executing projects alongside him. Profit and leading metrics are moving up faster because of you By 12 months: You are Ops Manager’s go to operator & on track to become Ops Manager. Nothing important moves in Ops without you knowing. You own the Asana board, key ops projects, and reporting cadence. You’re the person we trust to “just handle it,” and your comp reflects that increased ownership. If you become that go to operator, you’ll have real say in how we run Ops – you won’t just be ‘executing tickets,’ you’ll help design the system.” Who This Is NOT For You prefer to ‘coordinate’ and assign tasks to others instead of doing the work yourself with excellence. You want to manage people before you’ve truly proven you can personally execute at a high level. You want a chill, low-pressure 9–5 You need to be told what to do all day and hate being judged by objective numbers You mark tasks complete without proof or next steps You change jobs every 6–18 months and blame the company/manager/market/ You get defensive or freeze when given direct feedback or pressure You are currently juggling multiple full time clients and want to “squeeze us in” on the side. You are mass applying to dozens of jobs and just want to see who bites first. Who This IS For You’ve stayed 2–3+ years in at least one role and can prove outcomes You like pressure, highly competitive environments, being the one who “gets it done” when others stall You’ve built systems (trackers, automations, SOPs), not just followed them You are tech-comfortable: Asana (or similar), CRMs, zaps, AI tools, simple web/ops/marketing stacks You’re willing to bet on one company instead of juggling lots of smaller, easier gigs. You hate corporate BS– endless meetings, vague goals, and politics – and would rather be rewarded for what you actually create. You’re happy to grind 50–60 hours/week no issues. We’re in a BIG growth & push season. It will be like this for the next year and then we’ll see. Everyone wants to grow a lot, but it’s actually happening here. Comp & Growth (All of this is written into your contract.) Months 1–3: Ramp / Trial • $800/month base, guaranteed, while you learn our systems and we test fit. • No bonus in this phase. You’re paid to prove you can hit the KPI floors. Month 4+ – Performance Based Upside • Base stays at $800 until you’ve hit KPI floors for 2 straight months. After that, base increases to $900/month going forward. • On top of base, you can earn: $400 bonus in months where you hit 3 out of 4 KPIs (with Output as one of them). $1,000 bonus in months where you hit 4 out of 4 KPIs on the weekly scorecard. • In practice, that means: Solid performance months ~$1,200–$1,300/month Killer months (4/4 KPIs)~$1,800–$1,900/month All bonuses are 100% KPI based  (shipped outcomes, taking load off the Ops Manager, zero CEO/manager rescues, tight open loops) and 4/5 culture. Training & Growth Investment (on top of pay) We actively invest in making you a sharper teammate. Over time, we’ll put thousands of dollars into your development (courses, coaching, playbooks, and tools) that we choose together based on what will make you more effective in this seat. We also protect uninterrupted deep work blocks for you every week (no rando ---------- etings, no Slack spam). You’re paid to ship outcomes, not sit in back to back Zoom calls. Important: This is an ON FIELD role. You will not have a team under you to delegate to. 95% of your time is doing the work yourself, 5% is light coordination. If your default mode is to make plans and pass tasks to others, this will be a bad fit. Compensation here is performance based. Raises are earned through clearly exceeding KPIs and demonstrating core values consistently. If you want “stability” to mean “I can coast and still get raises,” this won’t feel stable. If you want stability to mean “the better I get, the more valuable and secure I become,” you’ll like it here. How To Apply (24-Hour Test) Our Hiring Process (So There Are No Surprises) If your 24 hour answers impress us, the next steps are: A short interview focused on your past execution. A live 60 minute work trial inside our real tools where you’ll work directly with the Ops Manager. We do this because talk is cheap. If you don’t like being tested on real work before getting hired, this won’t be a fit. Do NOT click quick-apply. In the next 24 hours, you must: Reply with answers to ALL of these (short but specific; bullets are fine): Q1: Describe the most complex project you personally drove fro ---------- ssy start to completion where you did most of the execution yourself, not just assigning tasks. Include at least one example of how you set your own deadlines and moved forward when other people were slow to respond.” Q2: Share 3 links or screenshots (Google Docs, Sheets, Asana boards, trackers, automations, etc.) that you built yourself which show how you organize and drive work. Briefly explain each. Q3: You have 30 tasks due this week and realize you’ll miss 5. Walk me through, step-by-step, how you handle it with your manager and stakeholders. In a Google Doc, please: Rewrite these into clear tasks with: Owner (you or Ops Manager), Due Date (next 7–30 days), and a concrete Done Check + proof required. “Write your task descriptions as if you are committing: ‘I will do X by Y time. If Z doesn’t happen by [time], here’s my fallback.’ Generic ‘follow up / request access’ answers will fail you.” Put them in the order you’d actually do them and explain why in 3–5 bullet points. This role will report to our Chief Commercial Officer and work closely with our market teams, revenue management, onboarding, field operations, and external marketing partners. This is a hands-on marketing role focused on listing optimization, channel content quality, website updates, homeowner acquisition marketing, referral channel support, brand consistency, and select social media support. The ideal candidate is a strong writer, comfortable with digital tools, highly organized, and excited to help build scalable marketing processes for a growing hospitality business. This role is especially important because our listings, websites, homeowner-facing content, and referral channels directly impact our ability to grow revenue, attract new homeowners, and create a premium brand experience across every market. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES LISTING OPTIMIZATION & CHANNEL CONTENT * Own the quality, consistency, and optimization of property listings across Guesty, Airbnb, Vrbo, Google Vacation Rentals, direct booking websites, and other distribution channels. * Write and refine listing titles, descriptions, summaries, photo captions, amenity highlights, and market-specific content. * Review listings for completeness, accuracy, conversion quality, and brand consistency. * Help determine the best hero images, photo order, captions, and property highlights for each listing. * Coordinate with market teams to confirm property details, amenities, local recommendations, and unique selling points. * Manage the listing optimization checklist for new and existing homes. * Support the launch of new listings by ensuring marketing content is complete, accurate, and on-brand before going live. * Review underperforming listings and recommend content, photo, or positioning improvements. * Manage the relationship with photography partners to help ensure property photography is high quality, consistent, and aligned with our brand standards. * Coordinate photography needs, shot lists, photo feedback, and follow-up requests with market teams and external photographers. WEBSITE & DIRECT BOOKING SUPPORT * Maintain and update property pages, market pages, owner-facing pages, and other website content. * Ensure direct booking websites are accurate, polished, and aligned with current listings and brand standards. * Support the creation of landing pages for market-specific campaigns, homeowner acquisition, and referral partners. * Help improve website content for SEO, readability, and conversion. * Coordinate with website vendors or internal tea ---------- mbers when technical changes are needed. * Support updates to Google Business Profiles and other local search assets. HOMEOWNER ACQUISITION MARKETING * Support marketing efforts designed to attract new vacation rental homeowners. * Help create and maintain homeowner-facing materials, including one-pagers, brochures, market summaries, case studies, listing improvement examples, and sales support materials. * Support email campaigns, nurture sequences, and other marketing efforts for prospective homeowners. * Help package the EHP value proposition clearly across markets, including our approach to home care, revenue management, guest experience, and owner communication. * Create market-specific content that helps homeowners understand why our local teams are the right partner for their vacation rental. REFERRAL CHANNEL MARKETING * Support marketing efforts for referral partners, including real estate agents, brokers, developers, designers, contractors, and other local professionals who may refer homeowners to us. * Help create referral partner collateral, outreach materials, email campaigns, and follow-up content. * Maintain referral channel marketing assets and ensure they are professional, clear, and easy for partners to share. * Support the marketing side of our lifetime value of leads strategy, helping us stay visible and valuable to referral sources over time. * Coordinate with leadership and market teams to identify partner opportunities and create simple, repeatable campaigns. BRAND & CONTENT CONSISTENCY * Help maintain consistent brand voice, tone, and visual standards across all markets and channels. * Create and manage templates for listings, owner marketing, referral partners, social media, presentations, and website content. * Use tools like Canva and Google Workspace to produce clean, professional, on-brand marketing materials. * Ensure each local brand feels personal and market-specific while still reflecting the quality and standards of Elevated Hospitality Partners. title: Credentialing Specialist
description: About Handspring Health Handspring is a virtual mental health clinic for children, young adults, and families. We are dedicated to transforming mental healthcare for families through high-quality, accessible virtual therapy. About the Role The Credentialing Analyst will support the day-to-day management of provider credentialing, licensing, payer enrollment, and related operational systems. This role is ideal for someone who is highly organized, comfortable working with data and trackers, and able to spot gaps, inconsistencies, and next steps across multiple systems. This is an analytical operations role. The person in this role will not just complete tasks, but will also help maintain clean data, monitor workflow progress, identify blockers, and give the team clear visibility into credentialing status. Key Responsibilities Maintain accurate provider credentialing and licensing data across internal trackers, spreadsheets, shared drives, and external systems. Review provider files for missing, outdated, or inconsistent information. Track credentialing, licensing, payer enrollment, recredentialing, renewal, and CAQH attestation deadlines. Update and maintain CAQH profiles, payer portals, NPI records, license documentation, malpractice insurance records, and other provider files. Prepare, submit, and track credentialing and payer enrollment applications under the direction of the operations team. Monitor provider status across credentialing workflows and flag delays, blockers, or missing items. Create and update reports showing credentialing status, upcoming deadlines, outstanding documents, payer enrollment progress, and other key workflow metrics. Reconcile information across systems to ensure provider records are accurate and consistent. Support provider onboarding by collecting, reviewing, and organizing required credentialing documents. Follow up with providers, internal tea ---------- mbers, and external organizations to move credentialing work forward. What We Are Looking For 3+ years of experience in healthcare credentialing, provider enrollment, licensing, payer operations, healthcare administration, or operations analysis. Strong spreadsheet skills and comfort maintaining detailed trackers. Experience working with U.S. healthcare credentialing workflows. Experience with CAQH ProView strongly preferred. Experience with payer portals, provider enrollment, NPI records, state licenses, malpractice documentation, and credentialing files preferred. Strong attention to detail and ability to identify inconsistencies across documents and systems. Comfort working independently in a remote environment. Strong written communication skills. Ability to manage recurring workflows, deadlines, and follow-ups without repeated reminders. Ability to handle confidential provider information with professionalism. Behavioral health, telehealth, therapy, or multi-state provider credentialing experience is a plus. Systems Experience Preferred CAQH ProView NPPES / NPI Registry Payer portals Google Sheets or Microsoft Excel Google Workspace Credentialing trackers or project management tools Shared drives and document management systems EHR or provider management systems Nice to Have Experience credentialing therapists, psychologists, social workers, or other behavioral health providers. Experience with multi-state licensing workflows. Experience supporting Medicaid, commercial insurance, or payer enrollment processes. Experience building or maintaining dashboards, trackers, or workflow reports. Experience working with offshore or distributed U.S.-based healthcare teams. Success in This Role Looks Like Credentialing data is accurate, complete, and consistently updated. The team has clear visibility into provider status, outstanding items, and next steps. Licensing, CAQH, payer enrollment, and recredentialing deadlines are tracked proactively. Provider files are organized, audit-ready, and easy to review. Workflow blockers are identified early and escalated appropriately. Trackers and reports are reliable enough for the team to use in weekly operations planning.

job_title: Executive Assistant-Right Hand-Fast-Growing Comic Book Company
description: Operations Manager-Execution Partner-Project Killer-Fast-Growing Comic Book Company Own the operations backbone of a niche comic book brand, work directly with leadership, and get promoted fairly by numbers. This role is for that special person who wants to become truly exceptional. If that’s you, you already know this message is your signal. What You Get If You Win Here - High autonomy: once you’re ramped, you own your queue, schedule, and methods as long as the KPIs are hit. Lots of freedom to figure it out, great for someone that loves building with Legos - Direct proximity to leadership: you work daily with the Ops Manager on the most important projects in the company. - Clear advancement path: your growth is tied to visible numbers (tasks shipped, zero-miss cadence, freed founder/ops time, profit/leading metrics), not politics. - Insane skill growth: the pace and standards here mean every 12 months with us will feel like 3 years of experience in a normal VA/ops role. You can leapfrog your friends. If you join this will change your life. You will work harder than you’ve ever worked before and grow faster than you’ve ever grown before. - Comic Books!: you’re not just pushing random SaaS tickets; you’re inside a real comic book store seeing rare old comic books, private deals, and the business behind the Hollywood Marvel Movies that everyone loves! If you’re that person who enjoys working really hard to the point that it takes 2-3 people to do what you did listen up: Our tasks in asana for projects and ongoing operations are moving at a snail’s pace. Ops Manager + CEO is chasing tasks, slack policing, cleaning up Asana, and re-explaining context instead of focusing on their jobs. We’ve had “pleasant” VAs who: Can’t drive tasks to completion independently Mark tasks complete with no proof Miss reports/skip cadence and require chasing. Drift on ownership, urgency & follow thru Need hand-holding I don’t need another task hopper. I need a project killer who comes into ambiguity, creates structure, drives tasks to completion, and actually frees the Ops Manager to focus on his key projects. If this works, his deep work hours and project output go up because you’re handling everything else. We will measure that and tie your promotions/raises to it. This is not for everyone. We’re looking for winners. What You’ll Actually Do You will be Ops Manager’s execution partner and force-multiplier. Concrete outputs: Own Asana: every task has an owner, due date, Done Check, and proof link when completed Maintain an active queue of 20+ meaningful tasks, prioritized against our key rocks (Marketing, Sales, Ongoing Operations, Cleanup, Admin) Ship 25+ tasks/week with proof, minimal rework, and zero “ghosted” items Proactively handle operational issues/fires in designated lanes Maintain Reporting at Set Cadence, Follow-up loops across projects Add leverage: plug AI into our workflows (Asana, docs, reports) to make us faster and cleaner without being asked We do NOT need more SOPS-although you might tighten them on the fly. We need someone to do the operations. If you want to sit and write playbooks all day, this is the wrong seat-that will be an earned responsibility later. If you aren’t ready to work hard daily do not apply. How We Set You Up To Win (First 90 Days) We don’t just throw you in the deep end. In your first 30 days, you’ll shadow the Ops Manager, learn our Asana + reporting systems, and get a clear scorecard so you always know what “great” looks like. By 30 days, you’ll own your own project lanes with weekly 1:1s for feedback, support, and removing blockers so you can move faster instead of guessing what we want. Real Growth Example One of our Filipino teammates started with us on basic execution work at ~$800/month. Over time, he took ownership of his queue, fixed broken processes, and became the person we trusted to “just handle it.” As his scope grew, so did his comp and stability. Now he makes ~$2,500/month (and we’re working on getting him even more) because he stuck with it and actually grew. A lot of people say they want that, but their resumes show 6–12 month hops. The pattern here is simple: prove you can own outcomes over time, and we grow your responsibilities, trust, and pay accordingly. Schedule, Hours & Time Zone (No Surprises) This is a full time, US hours role (roughly US Eastern business hours) with a true 50–60 hour workweek during this growth season. Expect most weeks to be closer to that 60 hour mark. If you want a strict 40 hour cap, this is the wrong seat; if you want a place where extra effort is noticed, measured, and rewarded, you’ll feel at home here. This is not just a job. This is a commitment. What Winning Looks Like By Day 30: Ops Manager is spending ~95% of his time on projects, not Slack/Asana/admin fires, because you’re handling those and executing projects alongside him. Profit and leading metrics are moving up faster because of you By 12 months: You are Ops Manager’s go to operator & on track to become Ops Manager. Nothing important moves in Ops without you knowing. You own the Asana board, key ops projects, and reporting cadence. You’re the person we trust to “just handle it,” and your comp reflects that increased ownership. If you become that go to operator, you’ll have real say in how we run Ops – you won’t just be ‘executing tickets,’ you’ll help design the system.” Who This Is NOT For You prefer to ‘coordinate’ and assign tasks to others instead of doing the work yourself with excellence. You want to manage people before you’ve truly proven you can personally execute at a high level. You want a chill, low-pressure 9–5 You need to be told what to do all day and hate being judged by objective numbers You mark tasks complete without proof or next steps You change jobs every 6–18 months and blame the company/manager/market/ You get defensive or freeze when given direct feedback or pressure You are currently juggling multiple full time clients and want to “squeeze us in” on the side. You are mass applying to dozens of jobs and just want to see who bites first. Who This IS For You’ve stayed 2–3+ years in at least one role and can prove outcomes You like pressure, highly competitive environments, being the one who “gets it done” when others stall You’ve built systems (trackers, automations, SOPs), not just followed them You are tech-comfortable: Asana (or similar), CRMs, zaps, AI tools, simple web/ops/marketing stacks You’re willing to bet on one company instead of juggling lots of smaller, easier gigs. You hate corporate BS– endless meetings, vague goals, and politics – and would rather be rewarded for what you actually create. You’re happy to grind 50–60 hours/week no issues. We’re in a BIG growth & push season. It will be like this for the next year and then we’ll see. Everyone wants to grow a lot, but it’s actually happening here. Comp & Growth (All of this is written into your contract.) Months 1–3: Ramp / Trial • $800/month base, guaranteed, while you learn our systems and we test fit. • No bonus in this phase. You’re paid to prove you can hit the KPI floors. Month 4+ – Performance Based Upside • Base stays at $800 until you’ve hit KPI floors for 2 straight months. After that, base increases to $900/month going forward. • On top of base, you can earn: $400 bonus in months where you hit 3 out of 4 KPIs (with Output as one of them). $1,000 bonus in months where you hit 4 out of 4 KPIs on the weekly scorecard. • In practice, that means: Solid performance months ~$1,200–$1,300/month Killer months (4/4 KPIs)~$1,800–$1,900/month All bonuses are 100% KPI based  (shipped outcomes, taking load off the Ops Manager, zero CEO/manager rescues, tight open loops) and 4/5 culture. Training & Growth Investment (on top of pay) We actively invest in making you a sharper teammate. Over time, we’ll put thousands of dollars into your development (courses, coaching, playbooks, and tools) that we choose together based on what will make you more effective in this seat. We also protect uninterrupted deep work blocks for you every week (no rando ---------- etings, no Slack spam). You’re paid to ship outcomes, not sit in back to back Zoom calls. Important: This is an ON FIELD role. You will not have a team under you to delegate to. 95% of your time is doing the work yourself, 5% is light coordination. If your default mode is to make plans and pass tasks to others, this will be a bad fit. Compensation here is performance based. Raises are earned through clearly exceeding KPIs and demonstrating core values consistently. If you want “stability” to mean “I can coast and still get raises,” this won’t feel stable. If you want stability to mean “the better I get, the more valuable and secure I become,” you’ll like it here. How To Apply (24-Hour Test) Our Hiring Process (So There Are No Surprises) If your 24 hour answers impress us, the next steps are: A short interview focused on your past execution. A live 60 minute work trial inside our real tools where you’ll work directly with the Ops Manager. We do this because talk is cheap. If you don’t like being tested on real work before getting hired, this won’t be a fit. Do NOT click quick-apply. In the next 24 hours, you must: Reply with answers to ALL of these (short but specific; bullets are fine): Q1: Describe the most complex project you personally drove fro ---------- ssy start to completion where you did most of the execution yourself, not just assigning tasks. Include at least one example of how you set your own deadlines and moved forward when other people were slow to respond.” Q2: Share 3 links or screenshots (Google Docs, Sheets, Asana boards, trackers, automations, etc.) that you built yourself which show how you organize and drive work. Briefly explain each. Q3: You have 30 tasks due this week and realize you’ll miss 5. Walk me through, step-by-step, how you handle it with your manager and stakeholders. Q4:  Below are 6 messy “tasks” we actually see (all dumped into one list): – “Fix Asana, it’s a mess” – “Seller lead texting follow up??” – “Finance com/projections cadence d2 ” – “Inventory backlog insane” – “Need better reporting” – “Update SOPs In this role you will NOT have anyone to delegate to assume it’s just you and the Ops Manager. 1. In a Google Doc, please: Rewrite these into clear tasks with: Owner (you or Ops Manager), Due Date (next 7–30 days), and a concrete Done Check + proof required. “Write your task descriptions as if you are committing: ‘I will do X by Y time. If Z doesn’t happen by [time], here’s my fallback.’ Generic ‘follow up / request access’ answers will fail you.” 2. Put them in the order you’d actually do them and explain why in 3–5 bullet points. 3. Link the Google Doc here (view access). Spend no more than 30–45 minutes. If you can’t figure this out on your own, this role will be too hard in real life – that’s okay, just skip applying. Attach your PDF resume/Google Drive link.

description: Hi! I’m looking for a reliable part-time E-commerce Operations Assistant to help with daily operations for a growing online store in the U.S. market. The business is expanding and I need someone hands-on who can help with customer communication, supplier follow-ups, product research, pricing checks, Shopify tasks, and keeping operations organized. We sell high-ticket products, not a simple one-product dropshipping item. We work with multiple brands and suppliers, and each brand can have different prices, margins, shipping rules, product details, lead times, warranties, and return policies. Many products are shipped directly from suppliers or manufacturers, so attention to detail is very important. This is a full time , but it is not a “work whenever you want” role. Since this position involves customer email s, SMS, calls, supplier follow-ups, abandoned checkout follow-ups, and order updates, you must have availability during agreed U.S. business hours, ideally between 9:00 AM and 5:00 PM Eastern Time. You will not be working full-time every day at the beginning, but you must be available during that working window when tasks, calls, or follow-ups are needed. This will start as a part-time, task-by-task role, but as the business grows and you prove you are reliable, the work can become more consistent. Pay can also increase as your performance improves and the business continues to grow. Main tasks may include: Responding to customer email s, SMS, and calls in English, including order updates, product questions, quote follow-ups, abandoned checkout follow-ups, and general customer support. Making and answering customer calls in English when needed. Following up with customers by call, SMS, or email for quotes, pending payments, abandoned checkouts, product questions, delivery updates, and order issues. Following up with suppliers about stock, pricing, shipping, product details, and lead times. Updating customers about order status, delivery updates, and supplier responses. Checking product prices, supplier costs, margins, and competitor pricing. Comparing our prices with U.S. competitors. Using a VPN when needed to view U.S. pricing, competitor websites, and availability. Helping with Shopify product uploads and product updates. Reviewing product pages for missing or incorrect information. Keeping CRM sheets and internal spreadsheets organized. Updating customer notes, supplier notes, order notes, and follow-up status. Helping with warranty, return, cancellation, and delivery communication. Handling customer problems professionally and knowing when to escalate an issue before making promises or decisions. Following SOPs and training videos for each task. You will not be expected to do everything at once. I will assign specific tasks and provide instructions, examples, and training videos when needed. Requirements Please do not apply if you do not think you qualify. Advanced written and spoken English. Confident speaking with U.S. customers by phone. Comfortable answering calls, making follow-up calls, replying to SMS, and handling customer issues professionally. Able to communicate clearly when there is a problem, delay, warranty issue, delivery concern, or customer complaint. Experience with Shopify, e-commerce operations, slack, customer support, or virtual assistant work. Experience using Google Sheets, CRM sheets, spreadsheets, or similar tools to stay organized. Able to work with the U.S. market and U.S. customers. Available during agreed U.S. business hours, ideally between 9:00 AM and 5:00 PM Eastern Time, depending on assigned tasks, calls, and follow-ups. Must have reliable internet. Must be able to use a VPN when needed. Strong attention to detail. Organized and able to keep accurate notes. Able to follow step-by-step instructions carefully. Comfortable checking supplier websites, product pages, pricing, shipping details, and competitor pages. Able to ask questions when something is unclear instead of guessing. Able to work with urgency when a task is assigned. Must understand that refunds, cancellations, discounts, returns, or compensation cannot be approved without owner approval. Important This business sells high-ticket products, so mistakes can be expensive. A wrong product detail, wrong price, missed follow-up, or incorrect promise to a customer can create serious problems. You should not promise customers exact delivery dates unless they are confirmed. You should not approve refunds, returns, cancellations, discounts, or compensation unless I specifically authorize it. You must be careful when checking prices because different brands have different margins, supplier costs, shipping fees, MAP rules, and competitor pricing. Examples of tasks you may receive “Check if this product is in stock with the supplier and confirm the shipping cost.” “Reply to this customer asking for a delivery update.” “Call this customer and confirm their shipping address.” “Call or text this customer who started checkout but did not complete the order.” “Follow up with this lead and ask if they have any questions before purchasing.” “Compare our price with this competitor and calculate the margin.” “Update the CRM sheet with the customer status and next follow-up.” “Check this Shopify order/customer profile and update the CRM sheet with the latest status.” “Check if this product page is missing warranty, shipping, or specification details.” “Upload these products to Shopify using this supplier page.” “Organize this supplier information in the supplier database.” “Follow up with this supplier about tracking or freight delivery.” “Review this customer issue and prepare a draft response.” How to apply Please message me here if you are interested. To show that you read the full post carefully, start your message with: “Hi Chris, I can help with U.S. e-commerce operations.” Also, somewhere in your application, mention: “CRM sheet” Please do not send a generic cover letter. Instead, answer these questions in your own words: Have you worked with Shopify, customer service, or e-commerce operations before? Explain briefly. Are you comfortable speaking with U.S. customers by phone in English? Are you available during U.S. business hours, ideally between 9:00 AM and 5:00 PM Eastern Time, for assigned tasks, calls, SMS, and follow-ups? Have you used Google Sheets,slack,  CRM sheets, or spreadsheets to manage customer/order information? A customer asks for an exact delivery date, but the supplier only gave an estimated transit time. How would you respond? Before telling a customer that a product is in stock, what would you check? If a customer asks for a refund, discount, cancellation, or compensation, what would you do before confirming anything? Are you able to use a VPN to check U.S. competitor pricing and product availability? Applications that do not follow these instructions will not be considered. Thanks! Chris

You'll work across multiple client accounts, so you should already have a vetted list of backlink sources and placements you've personally used with success. Experience: 2–5 years in link building or SEO Employment type: Full-time (contract options available) Focus areas: Link building + AEO/GEO + AI search & LLM citation Core link-building responsibilities Research and prospect link targets using Ahrefs, Semrush, and Moz — but prioritize niche relevance and real editorial traffic over raw DA/DR scores. A relevant link from a trade publication beats twenty links from high-authority sites no one reads Run journalist-source and digital-PR outreach (email , LinkedIn) using current platforms — Qwoted, Source of Sources (SOS), ---------- , and #JournoRequest on X (HARO/Connectively shut down in Dec 2024; don't rely on it) — to earn guest posts, editorial links, resource-page placements, and press coverage Conduct competitor backlink analysis to identify gaps and replicate genuinely earnable, high-value opportunities Monitor backlink profiles, identify toxic links, and submit disavow requests via Google Search Console Work with the content team to develop linkable assets — original data studies, surveys, infographics, and long-form guides that publishers actually want to cite Local citations & directory management Manually build and manage local citations and business directory listings across Canadian and North American platforms — the kind of work a tool like BrightLocal automates, done by hand for accuracy and full control Set up new accounts and complete listings from scratch where needed, keeping NAP (Name, Address, Phone) data consistent across every directory Work from a provided master list of target directories for manual entry, and proactively flag additional niche- or region-relevant directories worth adding Keep listings current over time — updating details, removing duplicates, and verifying entries AEO, GEO & LLM citation responsibilities Answer Engine Optimization (AEO): Optimize content to be selected as the direct answer in Google AI Overviews and AI Mode, Bing Copilot, Perplexity, voice assistants, and featured snippets Generative Engine Optimization (GEO): Ensure our brands, products, and content are accurately represented and cited in outputs from generative AI models including ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini Audit how — and whether — our brands are cited in LLM outputs (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity) and track citation frequency, accuracy, and sentiment over time Earn mentions and citations on the sources AI answer engines index most heavily — authoritative publications, industry wikis, Reddit, Quora, and reputable government/educational domains Note: many of these placements are "no-follow" and won't pass traditional link equity. For AEO/GEO that's expected — the goal is AI citation and entity strength, not PageRank. We want someone who understands that distinction. Structure content for extraction: lead with a direct 40–60 word answer block, use FAQ schema, speakable schema, and clear entity definitions, and write in an objective, declarative voice (AI engines down-weight "we think / in our opinion" hedging) Keep content fresh and specific — recency and concrete statistics are heavily weighted, especially by Perplexity, which refreshes near-daily and cites 4–8 sources per answer Make sure AI crawlers can actually read the page: critical text rendered server-side (not injected by client-side JavaScript), and the right crawler access configured (e.g. OAI-SearchBot for ChatGPT search eligibility, distinct from GPTBot training access) Develop and execute digital PR strategies aimed at earning mentions on high-E-E-A-T domains that serve as training and retrieval sources for AI models Strengthen entity recognition across AI systems by optimizing Knowledge Panels, Wikidata entries, and third-party review platforms (G2, Trustpilot, Clutch) How we work — our standards (non-negotiables) Link building in 2026 is about earning citations and trust, not gaming volume. We expect you to: Earn, don't manipulate. No PBNs, link farms, paid link networks, comment spam, or scaled/automated link schemes. Google's spam updates penalize these, and one bad shortcut can damage a client account we've spent months building. Manually vet every target. Real editorial standards, real organic traffic, real topical relevance — not just a metric in a tool. Disclose paid placements with rel="sponsored" where applicable. Build relationships, not one-offs. Repeat publisher relationships beat cold-blasting templates that editors delete on sight. Honour the human edit pass. title: Heir Outreach Specialist
description: We are hiring a confident, persuasive, and highly proactive Heir Outreach Specialist to help our real estate investment company contact property owners and heirs connected to distressed Florida properties. This is not a passive admin role. This role is for someone who enjoys starting conversations, moving people to action, asking direct questions, and staying calm when a family situation is complicated. Our business solves title problems involving inherited property, probate issues, tax deed risk, liens, judgments, and family ownership problems. Your job is to help us reach the right heirs, confirm family relationships, gather key facts, build trust quickly, and keep communication moving so our acquisitions and transaction teams can close deals. What You Will Do • Call, text, and follow up with heirs and property owners connected to inherited or distressed Florida real estate. • Start conversations confidently with people who may not be expecting your call. • Identify decision-makers inside families with multiple heirs, siblings, children, spouses, or extended relatives. • Ask clear fact-finding questions about family relationships, deceased owners, probate status, property history, occupancy, and seller motivation. • Build rapport quickly while still keeping the conversation focused and productive. • Overcome hesitation and confusion without being pushy, rude, or robotic. • Document every conversation accurately inside our CRM so the rest of the team knows exactly what happened and what needs to happen next. • Coordinate warm handoffs to the acquisitions team when a seller or heir is ready to discuss an offer. • Persistently follow up until the family situation is understood, the right person is reached, or the lead is properly disqualified. Who This Role Is Perfect For • You are naturally confident on the phone and do not freeze when someone is guarded, confused, emotional, or skeptical. • You like winning conversations, solving people puzzles, and figuring out who has authority inside a family. • You are comfortable being direct, but you know how to sound respectful and human. • You move fast, follow up aggressively, and do not need to be reminded five times to complete the next step. • You prefer clear goals, measurable results, and real responsibility over repetitive low-impact admin work. • You can handle messy information, incomplete family trees, and leads where the first person you reach is not the final decision-maker. • You are energized by the challenge of turning cold or lukewarm contacts into productive conversations. You Will Not Be a Fit If • You are uncomfortable making outbound calls or speaking with strangers. • You need every step scripted before you can take action. • You avoid difficult conversations or give up after one unanswered call. • You are careless with notes, names, dates, phone numbers, or relationship details. • You sound overly timid, overly formal, or robotic on the phone. • You prefer back-office data entry and do not want to be accountable for outreach results. Required Skills • Strong spoken English with a clear, confident, professional phone presence. • Experience with outbound calling, sales, appointment setting, customer service, collections, real estate, legal intake, probate, or lead follow-up is strongly preferred. • Ability to ask questions, listen carefully, and control the direction of a conversation. • Comfortable using CRM systems, spreadsheets, Google Workspace, WhatsApp, and phone software. • Fast and accurate note-taking after calls and text conversations. • Stable internet connection, quiet work environment, and reliable computer. • High ownership: you follow through without needing constant supervision. Real Estate / Probate Experience You do not need to be an expert in Florida probate or curative title work before starting. We will train the right person on our lead types, terminology, workflows, and CRM process. However, you must be a fast learner, comfortable with complex family situations, and willing to study the business so you can improve quickly. Performance Expectations • Make consistent outbound calls, texts, and follow-ups during assigned work hours. • Reach heirs, confirm relationships, and identify the right decision-makers. • Maintain clean CRM records after every meaningful interaction. • Move qualified leads forward quickly instead of letting them sit idle. • Communicate daily progress, blockers, and next-step recommendations to the team. • Demonstrate measurable improvement in call quality, contact rate, lead qualification, and handoffs over time. Training and Support • Call scripts, talk tracks, and objection-handling guidance. • Training on inherited property, heirs, probate-related terminology, and title problems. • CRM workflow training and lead status definitions. • Daily or weekly coaching based on actual calls, notes, and results. • Clear success metrics so you always know what winning looks like. Work Schedule This role requires availability during U.S. calling hours. Exact schedule can be discussed, but strong candidates should be available for meaningful overlap with Central Time business hours. Consistent attendance, responsiveness, and daily execution are required. Compensation $5/hr + $250 bonus per deal closed How to Apply To apply, send an email to ---------- with the subject line: “Heir Outreach - I Can Move Leads Forward” • A short summary of your outbound calling, sales, real estate, legal, probate, collections, or lead follow-up experience. • A 60- to 90-second voice recording introducing yourself and explaining why you would be effective in this role. • Your available work hours in Central Time. • DISC test results: ---------- • A brief answer to this question: “Tell me about a time you had to keep following up with someone who was hard to reach.
